Title: Malicious Chrome Extensions Distributing Adware and Traffic Fraud

Victim.Description: Users of Google Chrome who installed the malicious extensions.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a network of malicious Chrome extensions used for adware distribution and traffic fraud. The adversary is financially motivated, potentially originating from Turkey, and employs Chrome extensions to manipulate traffic signals and collect user data. The infrastructure includes multiple Chrome Web Store accounts and backend domains. Victims are global users of Google Chrome who installed these extensions.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a network of 152 Google Chrome extensions acting as new tab live wallpaper add-ons to distribute a potentially unwanted program (PUP) family. These extensions span 38 separate Chrome Web Store publisher accounts and three brand backends: tabplugins.com, yowgames.com, and chromewallpaper.com, collectively installed 105,000 times. Despite claims of not collecting user data, the extensions log IP addresses, ISP, click counts, and referrers, sharing data with Google AdSense, DoubleClick, and third-party ad partners. A sub-cluster of extensions defines two hard-coded URLs in a JavaScript file activated during install and uninstall operations, fabricating traffic origin signals. The campaign is assessed as a financially motivated commercial adware and traffic-attribution-fraud affiliate operation, potentially originating from Turkey.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance of Chrome Web Store policies, followed by weaponization through the development of malicious extensions. Delivery occurs via the Chrome Web Store, exploiting user trust to install the extensions. Once installed, the extensions collect data and manipulate traffic signals, communicating with backend servers for data exfiltration. The final objective is adware distribution and traffic fraud.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names such as tabplugins.com, yowgames.com, and chromewallpaper.com, which are critical for the operation of the malicious extensions. The extensions themselves act as tools for adware distribution and traffic fraud. No specific IP addresses or file hashes were identified, limiting the ability to disrupt the adversary's operations.

doc_summary: Palo Alto Networks has identified active exploitation of a PAN-OS vulnerability, CVE-2026-0257, by an unknown threat actor. This authentication bypass flaw affects GlobalProtect portals and gateways, allowing unauthorized VPN connections. Initial exploitation was observed on May 17, 2026. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has added this vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, urging mitigation by June 1, 2026. No post-access behavior or lateral movement has been detected. Palo Alto Networks has released indicators of compromise and recommends searching GlobalProtect logs for specific client configuration values.

The exploitation allows unauthorized VPN connections, posing a high risk to affected organizations.

Title: Sniper Dz Phishing Campaign Targeting Middle East and North Africa

Victim.Description: Victims were users in the Middle East and North Africa, targeted through social media.

diamond_model_summary: The Sniper Dz campaign targeted users in the Middle East and North Africa using social engineering and phishing techniques. The adversary leveraged a phishing-as-a-service platform to impersonate trusted entities and lure victims into a monetization funnel. The infrastructure included link aggregation platforms and a shared push-notification ecosystem. Victims were primarily in the telecommunications sector, with high exposure potential due to the widespread use of social media and mobile devices.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers from Group-IB disclosed a phishing campaign targeting users in the Middle East and North Africa. The campaign used fraudulent Facebook accounts impersonating politicians and organizations to promote fake offers. Victims were redirected through intermediary websites to phishing and traffic monetization infrastructure. The campaign was linked to Sniper Dz, a phishing-as-a-service platform dismantled by INTERPOL. Techniques included browser notification abuse, premium SMS subscriptions, and investment scams. The campaign exploited trusted platforms like Linkbio and Linktree, using VAPID keys for push notifications. The attack involved social engineering, history manipulation, and tab-under techniques to trap users and monetize traffic.
kill_chain_summary: The Sniper Dz campaign followed a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance through social media to identify targets. Weaponization involved creating fraudulent accounts and phishing pages. Delivery was executed via social media posts with malicious links. Exploitation and installation were achieved through browser notification abuse. Command and control utilized a shared push-notification ecosystem. Actions on objectives focused on monetization through premium-rate services and scams. The campaign demonstrated a sophisticated use of social engineering and legitimate web technologies to achieve its objectives.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Sniper Dz campaign's pyramid of pain includes domain names like linkbio and linktree, which were used for redirection and monetization. The use of a shared push-notification ecosystem with VAPID keys indicates a reliance on network host artifacts. The campaign's techniques, such as social engineering and phishing, represent TTPs that are challenging to change. The pyramid of pain highlights the adversary's strategic use of legitimate platforms and browser features to evade detection and maintain persistence.

Title: Dismantling of Outsider Enterprise Phishing Operation

Victim.Description: Victims include Android users receiving phishing SMS messages.

diamond_model_summary: The Outsider Enterprise operation represents a sophisticated phishing-as-a-service model, leveraging AI and a vast infrastructure of fake websites to impersonate trusted brands. The adversary, based in China, targeted global users, primarily through SMS phishing, resulting in significant financial losses. The operation's infrastructure included thousands of domains and a Telegram bot for coordination.
doc_summary: The FBI, in collaboration with Google and Black Lotus Labs, dismantled a large-scale Chinese phishing-as-a-service operation known as Outsider Enterprise. This operation involved thousands of phishing websites and AI-assisted phishing kits impersonating trusted brands via SMS through AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon. Active since at least 2023, Outsider Enterprise was linked to 9,000 fake websites and over a million fraudulent URLs, resulting in the theft of more than 3.8 million credit card records and $1.9 billion in losses. The FBI's Operation Riptide seized multiple servers, a Shopify storefront, and a Telegram bot associated with the operation. Google filed a civil lawsuit targeting the infrastructure and is working with telecom providers to block fraudulent messages. The Stop SCAMS Act is proposed to enhance anti-scam strategies in the United States.
kill_chain_summary: The Outsider Enterprise operation followed a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify targets, followed by weaponization through the development of phishing kits. Delivery was executed via SMS, leading to exploitation through user interaction with phishing links. The operation's objectives were achieved through the collection and use of stolen data for financial gain.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the Outsider Enterprise operation includes domain names as a significant indicator, with 9,000 fake websites identified. The use of AI and phishing kits represents tools and TTPs employed by the adversary. The operation's infrastructure, including a Telegram bot, adds to the complexity of detection and response efforts.

Title: Cyberattack on Saydel Community School District by Former IT Employee

Victim.Description: Saydel Community School District in Iowa was targeted.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves Ezekiel Dean Potter, a former IT employee, who conducted a cyberattack against Saydel Community School District. Potter retained access credentials and used them to disrupt operations, delete accounts, and cause financial damage. The attack leveraged VPN services for evasion and targeted educational platforms and user accounts.
doc_summary: Ezekiel Dean Potter, a former IT employee at Saydel Community School District in Iowa, conducted a prolonged cyberattack against his former employer. The attack disrupted classroom operations, deleted accounts, and caused significant financial damage. Potter retained access credentials after his employment ended and targeted the district's systems over 21 months. He deleted the district's Facebook page, stripped employees of access to educational platforms, and attempted to reset usernames and passwords. The attacks impaired the district's ability to teach and resulted in tens of thousands of dollars in remediation costs. Potter accessed the district's Apple School Manager account, deleting user accounts and device management data, which disabled management of district MacBooks and iPads. Unauthorized access attempts were also made against the district's GoDaddy account and other services. Potter used a VPN service to evade detection, but federal investigators traced activity to IP addresses associated with his other employers. He pleaded guilty to computer fraud charges and was sentenced to 21 months in prison, with restitution required.
kill_chain_summary: The attack began with Potter retaining access credentials after his employment ended, allowing him to conduct reconnaissance. He exploited these credentials to access systems and used VPN services to evade detection. Potter's actions on objectives included deleting accounts and disrupting operations, causing significant impact on the school district.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the use of VPN services and credential abuse as key tactics. No specific hashes, IP addresses, or domains were identified, but the use of valid accounts and VPNs indicates a medium level of sophistication. The attack caused significant disruption and financial damage to the victim organization.

Title: Operation Highland: Velvet Ant's Decade-Long Espionage Campaign

Victim.Description: A large organization with isolated critical infrastructure targeted by Velvet Ant.

diamond_model_summary: Operation Highland, attributed to the Velvet Ant group, involved a decade-long cyberespionage campaign targeting critical infrastructure. The adversary demonstrated high sophistication, exploiting a zero-day in NX-OS and deploying custom tools for persistence and credential theft. The infrastructure included modified Nginx configurations and a custom SOCKS5 proxy, while the victim was a large organization with isolated critical infrastructure.
doc_summary: Operation Highland, attributed to the Velvet Ant cyberespionage group, involved Chinese hackers compromising a target organization's authentication stack and maintaining persistence for 10 years. The campaign began in 2016, targeting vulnerable internet-facing systems before pivoting to an air-gapped environment. Velvet Ant exploited a zero-day in NX-OS on Nexus switches, deployed a modified GS-Netcat reverse shell, and installed a custom SOCKS5 proxy. They modified Nginx configurations to proxy requests to a FastCGI process, enabling remote execution. The attackers replaced legitimate PAM modules and OpenSSH components with backdoored versions, capturing credentials and logging commands. Sygnia researchers documented the campaign in 2024, highlighting the complexity of remediation due to extensive modifications to critical components.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for Operation Highland began with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable systems, followed by weaponization of a zero-day exploit in NX-OS. Delivery involved exploiting internet-facing servers, leading to installation of a modified GS-Netcat reverse shell and custom SOCKS5 proxy. Command and control was maintained through encrypted channels, while actions on objectives focused on long-term persistence and credential theft.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for Operation Highland includes domain names and network host artifacts as key indicators. Velvet Ant's use of a hardcoded relay domain and modified Nginx configurations for remote execution are significant. The group's custom tools, such as the modified GS-Netcat reverse shell and custom SOCKS5 proxy, further complicate detection and response efforts.

Title: Credential Stealer Attack on Arch User Repository (AUR)

Victim.Description: The primary victims were users of the Arch User Repository (AUR) who installed or updated compromised packages.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to trust in package management

diamond_model_summary: The attack on the Arch User Repository (AUR) involved an adversary exploiting the trust model by adopting orphaned packages and modifying build scripts to install a Rust-based credential stealer. The adversary's capability included deploying an eBPF rootkit for persistence and evasion. The infrastructure utilized a Tor onion service for command and control, while the victims were primarily users of the AUR, exposing developer workstations and build systems to credential theft.
doc_summary: In June 2023, attackers compromised over 400 packages in the Arch User Repository (AUR), modifying build scripts to install a Rust-based credential stealer. The malware, capable of deploying an eBPF rootkit, targeted developer secrets and used a Tor onion service for command and control. The attack exploited the trust model of AUR by adopting orphaned packages and spoofing git commit metadata. The primary payload was delivered via the npm package atomic-lockfile, with a secondary wave using js-digest. The incident highlights vulnerabilities in supply chain security, emphasizing the need for vigilance in package management systems.
kill_chain_summary: The attack followed a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify orphaned packages in the AUR. Weaponization involved modifying build scripts to include malicious npm packages. Delivery occurred through the AUR, exploiting the trust model for execution. Installation was achieved by deploying a systemd service for persistence. Command and control were maintained via a Tor onion service, while actions on objectives focused on harvesting developer credentials and potential cryptomining.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes hash values for the main payload, domain names like temp.sh for data exfiltration, and tools such as atomic-lockfile and js-digest. The adversary's tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) involved supply chain compromise and credential theft. The use of a Tor onion service for command and control adds complexity to detection and response efforts, highlighting the need for robust monitoring and threat intelligence capabilities.

Title: Authentication Bypass Vulnerability in phpBB Forum Software

Victim.Description: phpBB forum administrators and users.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a vulnerability in phpBB forum software, discovered by Aikido. The vulnerability allows attackers to bypass authentication and gain access to user accounts, including administrative privileges. The flaw affects phpBB versions 3.x and 4.x, and exploitation requires no special configuration. The vulnerability was reported on June 2, 2023, and addressed by phpBB on June 6, 2023. Administrators are advised to upgrade to version 3.3.17 or the master branch for 4.x releases.
doc_summary: A 10-year-old authentication bypass vulnerability was discovered in phpBB forum software, allowing attackers to log in as any user, including administrators. The flaw, found by Aikido security researchers, affects phpBB versions 4.0.0-a2 or 3.3.16 and below. It was reported on June 2, 2023, and addressed by phpBB on June 6, 2023. The vulnerability is trivial to exploit with a single HTTP request and does not require special configuration. Exploitation could allow attackers to view private messages, modify content, and impersonate staff. Remote code execution is not possible due to a separate password check. Administrators are advised to upgrade to version 3.3.17 or the master branch for 4.x releases. The update may affect OAuth authentication due to changes in the redirect handler location.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves the exploitation of an authentication bypass vulnerability in phpBB forum software. The vulnerability allows attackers to log in as any user, including administrators, without special configuration. This exploitation stage is critical as it provides unauthorized access to sensitive data and administrative functions. The vulnerability was reported by Aikido on June 2, 2023, and addressed by phpBB on June 6, 2023. Administrators are advised to upgrade to mitigate the risk.

The lack of specific indicators makes detection challenging, emphasizing the importance of timely software updates.

diamond_model_summary: Velvet Ant, a sophisticated China-nexus group, has been active since 2016, targeting Linux login systems by backdooring PAM and OpenSSH components. Their strategic objective is to maintain long-term access to critical infrastructure components.
doc_summary: Velvet Ant, a China-nexus cyber espionage group, has been active since 2016, compromising Linux login systems by backdooring PAM and OpenSSH components. The group targeted isolated networks by staging through internet-facing systems. They replaced trusted login programs with backdoored versions, allowing unauthorized access and credential logging. In 2024, Velvet Ant exploited a Cisco NX-OS vulnerability, CVE-2024-20399, to plant backdoors on switches. The group also used F5 BIG-IP appliances as internal command servers. Operation Highland highlights the need for integrity checks on trusted infrastructure components. Sygnia tracks Velvet Ant's activities, emphasizing the importance of verifying login software integrity.
kill_chain_summary: Velvet Ant's attack involves reconnaissance to identify vulnerable systems, weaponization by modifying trusted login programs, delivery through backdoored PAM and OpenSSH components, exploitation for unauthorized access, installation of persistent backdoors, command and control via compromised systems, and actions on objectives by logging credentials and maintaining access.

doc_summary: Google has initiated legal action against a Chinese cybercrime network accused of using its Gemini AI to conduct phishing attacks targeting Americans. doc_summary: Supply-chain attacks involve malicious packages, compromised software updates, or breaches involving trusted vendors. Early warning signs may appear in underground forums advertising GitHub access, private repositories, source code, API keys, OAuth tokens, cloud credentials, or CI/CD data. A software supply-chain attack targets trusted tools, vendors, software components, services, or processes. Once attackers compromise something trusted, they may reach downstream customers or internal systems. Flare researchers observed GitHub-related access sales, exposing secrets, deployment scripts, package publishing logic, cloud credentials, and CI/CD workflows. The April 2026 incident involved a trusted third-party AI tool and OAuth-connected SaaS access. The Sportradar AG case linked to a compromised Trivy scanner exposed sensitive operational material. TeamPCP sold alleged Mistral AI repositories, illustrating source-code theft risks. Shai-Hulud npm attack showed compromised maintainer accounts and malicious package updates. LiteLLM incident involved unauthorized PyPI package publishes. Malicious VS Code extensions showed development tools as attack vectors. Security teams should monitor for exposed developer credentials, GitHub access, package registry tokens, leaked repositories, CI/CD secrets, cloud keys, OAuth grants, and claims involving important vendors.

Title: Agentjacking Attack Exploiting AI Coding Agents via Sentry

Victim.Description: Organizations using AI coding agents integrated with Sentry are at risk.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to implicit trust in AI agents

diamond_model_summary: The Agentjacking attack leverages the implicit trust AI coding agents place in Sentry error events to execute arbitrary code on developer machines. The adversary, identified as Tenet Security, exploits this vulnerability to access sensitive data without direct interaction with the victim's infrastructure. The attack highlights the need for enhanced security measures in AI-driven development environments.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers from Tenet Security have identified a new class of attack called Agentjacking, which targets AI coding agents by exploiting a vulnerability in Sentry, an open-source error-tracking platform. The attack involves crafting fake error reports that trick AI agents into executing arbitrary code on developer machines. This method bypasses traditional security measures like EDR and firewalls, as it leverages the implicit trust AI agents place in Sentry's error events. The attack can lead to the exposure of sensitive data such as environment variables, Git credentials, and developer identities. Despite acknowledging the issue, Sentry has not fixed the vulnerability, citing technical defensibility challenges. The attack has been tested against over 100 organizations, achieving an 85% success rate. This incident highlights the growing attack surface presented by AI coding agents and the need for enhanced security measures in AI-driven development environments.
kill_chain_summary: The Agentjacking attack follows a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify organizations using Sentry and AI coding agents. The adversary then weaponizes fake error reports to exploit the AI agents' trust, delivering the payload via Sentry's infrastructure. Exploitation occurs when the AI agent executes the arbitrary code, leading to data exfiltration. The attack bypasses traditional security measures, emphasizing the need for improved detection and remediation strategies.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Agentjacking attack presents challenges in detection due to the lack of traditional indicators like hashes or IP addresses. Instead, it relies on exploiting the trust AI coding agents place in Sentry error events. This highlights the need for organizations to focus on behavioral analysis and anomaly detection to identify such attacks. The attack's reliance on implicit trust and legitimate infrastructure makes it difficult to detect using conventional methods.

doc_summary: Security researcher Chaotic Eclipse, also known as Nightmare-Eclipse and MSNightmare, has released a new Windows BitLocker bypass exploit named GreatXML. Title: Miasma Credential-Stealing Attack Framework Incident

diamond_model_summary: The Miasma incident involves an unknown adversary leveraging a sophisticated supply chain attack framework to compromise developer accounts and repositories. The adversary's capability includes the use of GitHub commit search for command and control, and the infrastructure involves compromised public registries and GitHub repositories. doc_summary: The Miasma credential-stealing attack framework was briefly made available for free on GitHub, after multiple repositories with the name 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release' began appearing since June 8, 2026. According to SafeDep, the source code has been published through compromised developer accounts. The Miasma codebase appears to be larger than a supply chain worm, allowing the operator to execute various attacks via stolen credentials against arbitrary or targeted packages on public registries (PyPI, npm, RubyGems), JFrog Artifactory, GitHub repositories and GitHub Actions, AI coding tools config poisoning, SSH-based lateral movement, and other attack vectors. The malware employs three independent C2 channels using GitHub commit search, each with a different search string and crypto key. Miasma is assessed to be a variant of the Shai-Hulud worm. The campaign has since morphed into a Python variant called Hades, impacting a total of 304 components.
kill_chain_summary: The Miasma attack framework follows a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable developer accounts, followed by weaponization of the Miasma framework for supply chain attacks. The framework allows for credential theft and lateral movement, posing a significant threat to the technology sector.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves adversaries using AI-driven tools to rapidly discover and exploit vulnerabilities in critical software. The adversaries are highly sophisticated, motivated by financial gain and disruption, and leverage tools like Claude Mythos Preview for vulnerability discovery. The infrastructure targeted is global, affecting organizations in the technology and software sectors. Victims face high impact severity due to the rapid exploitation of vulnerabilities.
doc_summary: In 2026, AI-driven tools like Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview discovered over 10,000 high-severity vulnerabilities in critical software, drastically reducing the time-to-exploit window from months to hours. AWS reported widespread exploitation using weak credentials and autonomous offensive tools, affecting over 600 devices globally. The Verizon 2026 DBIR highlighted a significant increase in vulnerability exploitation, with AI coding assistants enabling attackers to build and port exploits rapidly. Traditional patching processes struggle to keep pace, leading to increased breaches. Breach and Attack Simulation (BAS) and autonomous penetration testing are recommended to validate defenses and prioritize remediation. Picus Security's platform offers machine-speed defense by simulating real-world attacks and providing actionable insights.

Delivery occurs via automated tools exploiting weak credentials, leading to exploitation of vulnerabilities for client execution. Traditional defenses struggle to keep pace, necessitating the use of Breach and Attack Simulation and autonomous penetration testing to validate defenses and prioritize remediation efforts.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident highlights the challenge of defending against AI-driven attacks. Title: Miasma Credential-Stealing Attack Framework Leak

Victim.Description: Developers and organizations using open-source ecosystems are targeted.

diamond_model_summary: The Miasma attack framework represents a sophisticated adversary targeting open-source ecosystems through supply-chain attacks. The adversary uses GitHub as command-and-control infrastructure, leveraging credential theft and self-propagation to compromise developer environments. The leak of Miasma's source code on GitHub indicates a deliberate release by threat actors, potentially leading to more advanced variants and significant consequences for open-source security.
doc_summary: The Miasma credential-stealing attack framework, an evolution of the Shai-Hulud worm, has been leaked on GitHub, targeting open-source ecosystems through supply-chain attacks. The malware infects developer machines, steals credentials, and compromises repositories, publishing trojanized packages. It uses GitHub as command-and-control infrastructure, harvesting credentials from cloud providers, CI/CD systems, and more. A dead-man switch executes destructive commands if a stolen GitHub token is revoked. The five-stage build pipeline generates unique payloads, complicating detection. The leak is expected to lead to more advanced variants, impacting open-source security.
kill_chain_summary: The Miasma attack framework follows a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify targets within open-source ecosystems. Weaponization involves preparing unique payloads, followed by delivery through trojanized packages in repositories. Exploitation occurs via credential theft, leading to installation and persistence on victim machines. Command and control is achieved using GitHub, with actions on objectives focusing on credential theft and repository compromise.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Miasma attack framework presents challenges across the Pyramid of Pain, with unique hash values and domain names complicating detection. The use of GitHub as command-and-control infrastructure and the self-propagating nature of the malware increase the difficulty of mitigation. The framework's ability to generate unique payloads and employ obfuscation techniques further complicates detection and response efforts.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves attackers exploiting CVE-2026-5027, a path traversal vulnerability in Langflow, an AI development platform. doc_summary: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-5027, a high-severity path traversal vulnerability in Langflow, an AI development platform. The flaw allows arbitrary file writing on exposed servers due to improper sanitization of filenames in the 'POST /api/v2/files' endpoint. Tenable disclosed the issue on March 27, 2026, and a patch was released on March 30, 2026. VulnCheck's Caitlin Condon reported exploitation by attackers, facilitated by Langflow's default unauthenticated auto-login. Censys scans identified approximately 7,000 exposed instances. The Iranian threat group MuddyWater is linked to similar activities. Langflow users are advised to upgrade to the latest version.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance, where attackers likely scan for exposed Langflow instances. Exploitation follows, leveraging CVE-2026-5027 to gain initial access by writing arbitrary files on vulnerable servers. The exploitation is facilitated by Langflow's default unauthenticated auto-login, allowing attackers to proceed without credentials. The incident highlights the importance of patching and securing AI development environments.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the exploitation of CVE-2026-5027, a high-severity vulnerability in Langflow. The botnet's architecture uses Tor nodes for command-and-control, enabling stealthy operations. Title: RoguePlanet Zero-Day Exploit in Microsoft Defender

Victim.Description: The exploit affects Windows 11 and 10 machines with the June 2026 Patch Tuesday updates.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves Chaotic Eclipse, an anonymous researcher, who released a PoC exploit for a Microsoft Defender zero-day vulnerability named RoguePlanet. The exploit targets a race condition, allowing SYSTEM-level privilege escalation on Windows 11 and 10 machines. The adversary's motivation appears to be retaliation against Microsoft for alleged mishandling of vulnerability disclosures. The exploit was publicly disclosed on GitHub, highlighting tensions between independent researchers and Microsoft over vulnerability disclosure processes.
doc_summary: The anonymous security researcher known as Chaotic Eclipse, also referred to as Nightmare-Eclipse, released a proof-of-concept exploit for a Microsoft Defender zero-day vulnerability named RoguePlanet. The exploit, which is a race condition, can result in a shell with SYSTEM-level privileges on Windows 11 and 10 machines with the June 2026 Patch Tuesday updates. The exploit does not currently work on Windows Server instances. Chaotic Eclipse has expressed dissatisfaction with Microsoft's handling of vulnerability disclosures, leading to uncoordinated public disclosures. Microsoft has condemned these actions, stating they put customers at risk. The public feud has resulted in the takedown of Chaotic Eclipse's GitHub and GitLab accounts. Security researcher Will Dormann confirmed the exploit's effectiveness on the first attempt. The incident highlights tensions between independent researchers and Microsoft over vulnerability disclosure processes.
kill_chain_summary: The RoguePlanet exploit follows a sequence of stages in the MITRE ATT&CK framework. The weaponization stage involved developing a PoC exploit for the vulnerability. The delivery stage was marked by the public disclosure of the exploit on GitHub. Exploitation occurs when the race condition in Microsoft Defender is leveraged to gain SYSTEM-level privileges. The actions on objectives stage allows execution of arbitrary code with elevated privileges. The incident underscores the risks associated with public vulnerability disclosures.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the RoguePlanet incident includes the exploit itself as a tool, with no specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names identified. The exploit targets a race condition in Microsoft Defender, allowing SYSTEM-level privilege escalation. The public disclosure of the exploit increases the difficulty of detection and remediation, as it provides adversaries with the means to exploit the vulnerability. The incident highlights the challenges of addressing zero-day vulnerabilities in widely used software.

Title: AI-Driven Worm Exploits Vulnerabilities in Isolated Network

Victim.Description: The test network, named 'FakeCorp', included 33 hosts with various operating systems and IoT devices.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves an AI-driven worm developed by researchers at the University of Toronto. The worm autonomously identifies and exploits vulnerabilities using a locally hosted large language model. It targets a deliberately vulnerable network, demonstrating high sophistication in autonomous reasoning and attack generation. The worm's infrastructure includes a 33-host network with various operating systems and IoT devices. The victim is a research network, and the impact severity is high due to the worm's ability to gain elevated access and replicate itself across the network.
doc_summary: University of Toronto researchers developed an AI-driven worm using a locally hosted large language model to autonomously navigate and exploit a network. The worm identified vulnerabilities, gained elevated access, and replicated itself across a 33-host network, demonstrating the potential of AI in cyber threats. The worm's ability to generate attack logic at runtime without pre-encoded exploit chains or reliance on commercial AI services highlights a new frontier in cybersecurity challenges. The research, led by Nicolas Papernot, involved experiments on a deliberately vulnerable network, showcasing the worm's capability to exploit real-world vulnerabilities like SambaCry, Dirty Pipe, and PrintNightmare. The worm's adaptive nature, ability to ingest public advisories, and rewrite its code to bypass security controls underscore the evolving threat landscape. The study emphasizes the need for advanced defensive measures against AI-driven cyber threats.
kill_chain_summary: The AI-driven worm follows a comprehensive kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify vulnerabilities on the network. It then weaponizes by generating attack logic at runtime, followed by delivery of payloads to vulnerable hosts. Exploitation occurs as the worm gains elevated access, leading to installation on compromised hosts. Command and control are established through distributed reasoning using compromised hosts. Finally, the worm achieves its objectives by self-replicating and further exploiting the network. The worm's adaptive nature and ability to rewrite its code for evasion highlight its advanced capabilities.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes various indicators. Hash values and IP addresses are not specified, but the worm's use of a large language model and its ability to generate attack logic at runtime are significant tools. The worm's tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) include autonomous reasoning, runtime attack generation, and self-replication. These indicators highlight the worm's advanced capabilities and the challenges it poses for detection and remediation. The worm's ability to exploit vulnerabilities and rewrite its code for evasion further complicates defensive efforts.

Title: Exploitation of WinRAR Vulnerability CVE-2025-8088 by Russia-Aligned Groups

Victim.Description: Ukrainian organizations targeted by Russia-aligned cyber attack campaigns.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves two Russia-aligned groups, Earth Dahu and SHADOW-EARTH-066, exploiting a WinRAR vulnerability (CVE-2025-8088) to target Ukrainian organizations. The adversaries employ sophisticated techniques, including NTFS Alternate Data Streams and in-memory DLL loading, to deploy malware such as GIFTEDCROOK and GammaSteel. The infrastructure includes dedicated C2 servers for data exfiltration, and the victims are primarily Ukrainian organizations reliant on WinRAR. The severity of the incident is high due to the potential for significant data exfiltration and long-term access.
doc_summary: Two Russia-aligned cyber attack campaigns, Earth Dahu and SHADOW-EARTH-066, have been exploiting a security flaw in WinRAR, CVE-2025-8088, to target Ukrainian organizations. The vulnerability, a path traversal flaw allowing file writing outside the extraction directory via NTFS Alternate Data Streams, was patched in July 2025. SHADOW-EARTH-066 has shifted from Excel macro droppers to using crafted RAR archives with decoy PDFs and hidden ADS payloads to deliver the GIFTEDCROOK information stealer. The malware targets passwords and cookies from Chromium-based browsers and Mozilla Firefox, and exfiltrates data to external servers. Earth Dahu uses an HTA-to-VBScript infection chain to deliver espionage modules, deploying GammaPhish and GammaLoad to maintain long-term access. The convergence of these groups on a single vulnerability highlights the cyber threats facing Ukraine.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the weaponization of RAR archives containing decoy PDFs and hidden ADS payloads. These are delivered to target systems, exploiting the CVE-2025-8088 vulnerability in WinRAR. Upon exploitation, malware such as GIFTEDCROOK is installed, leveraging PowerShell for execution. Command and control is maintained through dedicated C2 servers, facilitating data exfiltration. The attackers employ defensive evasion tactics by deleting malicious artifacts post-exfiltration. The incident highlights the importance of patch management and user education to mitigate such threats.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes several indicators: malware hashes (GIFTEDCROOK, GammaPhish), IP addresses of C2 servers, domain names used for exfiltration, network host artifacts such as NTFS Alternate Data Streams, tools like PowerShell and cmd.exe, and TTPs including path traversal and in-memory DLL loading. These indicators provide varying levels of difficulty for adversaries to change, with TTPs being the most challenging. Effective detection and response strategies should focus on these high-impact indicators to disrupt the attack chain.

doc_summary: CISA has mandated U.S. government agencies to secure Check Point Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access deployments against a critical vulnerability exploited by Qilin ransomware affiliates. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to bypass authentication on Mobile Access/SSL VPNs, Remote Access VPNs, or Spark firewalls using the deprecated IKEv1 protocol. Check Point identified the exploitation beginning May 7, with attacks linked to Qilin Ransomware-as-a-Service, which has over 400 victims. CISA added CVE-2026-50751 to its directive, urging immediate patching. The vulnerability poses significant risks to federal enterprises, with mitigation measures including removing legacy client support, configuring IKEv2, enabling IPS, and mandating Machine Certificate Authentication.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of a Check Point VPN vulnerability, allowing unauthorized access. Title: FROST: SSD Timing Attack via JavaScript

doc_summary: FROST is a novel SSD timing attack developed by researchers at Graz University of Technology, exploiting the Origin Private File System (OPFS) in major desktop browsers. The attack uses JavaScript to infer user activity by measuring SSD contention, requiring no native code or permissions. It affects macOS and Linux, with high accuracy in identifying websites and apps. The attack leverages OPFS to bypass permission prompts, creating large files to force SSD reads. Detection is challenging, as the attack runs within the browser sandbox. Mitigation requires browser-level changes, such as capping OPFS size or introducing permission prompts. The attack highlights the risks of granting web apps near-native hardware access.
kill_chain_summary: FROST follows a structured attack chain, starting with the development of JavaScript code to exploit SSD timing via OPFS. The attack is delivered through a malicious webpage, exploiting SSD timing to infer user activity. It runs within the browser sandbox, evading detection, and collects information on user activity, demonstrating a high level of sophistication.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The FROST attack presents challenges in detection due to its reliance on SSD timing and JavaScript within the browser sandbox. Title: Hades Campaign: Malicious PyPI Packages and Credential Theft

Victim.Description: Targets include developers using PyPI packages, with a focus on computational biology and bioinformatics sectors.

diamond_model_summary: The Hades campaign is a sophisticated supply chain attack linked to the Miasma actor. It targets developers using PyPI packages, leveraging malicious artifacts to execute a JavaScript stealer. The campaign uses GitHub for payload hosting and exfiltration, with a focus on credential theft. The adversary employs advanced tactics, including AI evasion techniques and memory scraping on multiple operating systems.
doc_summary: The Hades campaign is a continuation of the Miasma supply chain attacks, targeting the Python Package Index (PyPI) with 37 malicious wheel artifacts across 19 packages. The campaign uses a *-setup.pth file to execute a payload during Python startup, downloading the Bun JavaScript runtime to run an obfuscated JavaScript stealer. This stealer harvests credentials from developer systems, including secrets from GitHub, npm, PyPI, and cloud services like AWS and Azure. The campaign introduces new tactics, such as using a plain-text prompt injection to deceive AI-based package analysis tools and querying GitHub for specific keywords to extract payloads. The malware also includes memory scraping capabilities for macOS and Windows systems. The campaign's severity is high, with significant implications for software supply chain security.

Weaponization involves creating malicious PyPI packages, followed by delivery through the PyPI registry. Exploitation occurs during Python startup, leading to the installation of the Bun runtime and execution of the stealer. Command and control is achieved via GitHub, with actions on objectives focusing on credential theft.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Hades campaign presents significant challenges for defenders, with a focus on supply chain compromise and credential theft. diamond_model_summary: The VerdantBamboo cyber espionage incident involved a sophisticated China-nexus threat actor deploying malware on Linux systems. The adversary used living-off-the-land techniques and customized persistence mechanisms to evade detection. The infrastructure included compromised Egnyte Storage Sync and Synology NAS systems, with the victim being an unnamed organization. The attack leveraged a local privilege escalation flaw and stolen credentials to access the victim's network.
doc_summary: A China-nexus cyber espionage group, VerdantBamboo, was observed deploying a BSD variant of the BRICKSTORM backdoor and two other malware families, PLENET (aka GRIMBOLT) and AGENTPSD, targeting Linux systems. The activity overlaps with groups known as Clay Typhoon, UNC5221, and Warp Panda. The intrusion was discovered during an incident response in September 2025, involving the compromise of an Egnyte Storage Sync system via a local privilege escalation flaw. The adversary accessed the victim's Microsoft 365 environment using the malware's proxying capabilities and compromised credentials. VerdantBamboo later breached the same organization using stolen administrative credentials to configure web SSL VPN access and deploy additional malware to a Synology NAS appliance. The threat actor also compromised the victim's Managed Services Provider, infecting its pfSense firewall with BRICKSTORM. The use of PLENET was reported by Google in connection with UNC6201, exploiting a Dell RecoverPoint vulnerability (CVE-2026-22769). VerdantBamboo employs living-off-the-land techniques and customized persistence mechanisms, leveraging limited domains and IPs per victim.
kill_chain_summary: The VerdantBamboo incident followed a structured kill chain, beginning with the exploitation of a local privilege escalation flaw in Egnyte Storage Sync systems. The adversary installed BRICKSTORM, PLENET, and AGENTPSD malware to maintain persistence. Command and control were achieved through compromised credentials and proxying capabilities. The attackers accessed the victim's Microsoft 365 environment and deployed additional malware to a Synology NAS appliance.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the VerdantBamboo incident includes several indicators. Hash values for the malware families BRICKSTORM, PLENET, and AGENTPSD are critical for detection. IP addresses and domain names used for command and control are also significant. Network host artifacts, such as compromised Egnyte Storage Sync and Synology NAS systems, provide further detection opportunities. The tools and TTPs employed by VerdantBamboo, including living-off-the-land techniques and customized persistence mechanisms, are crucial for understanding the threat actor's behavior.

The adversary, also known as Chatty Spider, Luna Moth, and Silent Ransom Group, targets professional, legal, and financial services in the United States. doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a financially motivated data theft extortion campaign by UNC3753, also known as Chatty Spider, Luna Moth, and Silent Ransom Group (SRG). The campaign targeted professional, legal, and financial services in the United States between January and May 2026. UNC3753 used voice phishing (vishing) and social engineering to gain remote access to corporate environments, posing as IT support to initiate screen-sharing sessions and install remote monitoring and management (RMM) utilities. The attackers exfiltrated proprietary legal agreements, personally identifiable information (PII), and financial records. In some cases, they accessed systems in person, posing as IT technicians. UNC3753 shares tactical overlaps with UNC2686 and has been linked to the now-defunct Conti ransomware gang. The group has used DNS Fast Flux infrastructure to make its domains harder to block.
kill_chain_summary: The MITRE ATT&CK kill chain analysis of the UNC3753 campaign identifies several stages: Reconnaissance involves identifying targets in the professional, legal, and financial sectors. Delivery is achieved through phishing emails that establish a pretext for voice calls. Installation occurs when victims are guided to install remote desktop software. Command and Control is maintained using DNS Fast Flux infrastructure. Actions on Objectives include data exfiltration and extortion demands. The campaign demonstrates a high level of sophistication, with the adversary leveraging social engineering and technical evasion tactics to achieve their objectives.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain analysis for the UNC3753 campaign highlights several indicators of compromise. The adversary uses DNS Fast Flux infrastructure, making domain names a significant pain point for defenders. Tools such as AnyDesk, Bomgar, and Zoho Assist are employed for remote access, adding complexity to detection efforts. The use of voice phishing and social engineering tactics represents a high level of sophistication, challenging defenders to identify and mitigate these threats. The campaign's reliance on legitimate software for persistence and data exfiltration further complicates detection and response efforts.

Title: C0XMO Botnet Targets DD-WRT Routers and Expands to Multiple Architectures
Tools: Brute-force tools for SSH and Telnet

Victim.Description: The primary victim identified is a Japanese technology company, with potential for broader targeting due to the botnet's capabilities.

diamond_model_summary: The C0XMO botnet represents a sophisticated adversary with advanced capabilities, targeting a range of devices across multiple architectures. Its modular design allows for flexible exploitation and lateral movement, primarily for launching DDoS attacks. The infrastructure includes a C2 server with a custom handshake, and the victim is a Japanese technology company. The botnet's persistence mechanisms and defensive evasion tactics highlight its operational complexity.
doc_summary: The C0XMO botnet, a new variant of Gafgyt, targets DD-WRT router firmware and other devices with various CPU architectures, including ARM, MIPS, PowerPC, SuperH, x86, and x86_64. Discovered by Fortinet researchers, C0XMO features a modular design allowing updates to exploitation techniques and lateral movement capabilities. It primarily launches DDoS attacks using 19 methods, such as UDP/TCP/SYN/ICMP floods and NTP/Memcached amplification. The botnet exploits CVE-2021-27137, a buffer overflow vulnerability, for arbitrary code execution. C0XMO downloads a Python script for network scanning and brute-force attacks on SSH and Telnet. It targets a Japanese technology company, with the source IP traced to Germany. The malware copies itself to hidden locations, creates cron jobs for persistence, and modifies shell startup files. It scans for competitor botnets and terminates them, connecting to a C2 server with a custom handshake. Recommendations include updating devices, using unique credentials, and disabling unnecessary remote access.
kill_chain_summary: The C0XMO botnet follows a comprehensive kill chain, starting with reconnaissance through network scanning and progressing to exploitation via CVE-2021-27137. It installs itself on compromised devices, maintains persistence through cron jobs, and connects to a C2 server for command and control. The botnet's primary objective is to launch DDoS attacks, employing various methods to achieve its goals. Defensive evasion is achieved by terminating competitor botnets and removing persistence mechanisms.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The C0XMO botnet's indicators of compromise include IP addresses, network host artifacts, and TTPs. The botnet's modular design and use of a custom C2 handshake make it challenging to detect and mitigate. Its ability to exploit vulnerabilities and maintain persistence across multiple architectures adds to the complexity of defending against it. The pyramid of pain scoring reflects the difficulty in addressing these indicators, emphasizing the need for robust detection and remediation strategies.

Title: OpenAI Introduces Lockdown Mode to Mitigate Prompt Injection Risks

Victim.Description: Potential victims include users and organizations handling sensitive data using ChatGPT.

diamond_model_summary: OpenAI's introduction of Lockdown Mode aims to mitigate data exfiltration risks from prompt injection attacks. The feature limits outbound network requests, enhancing security for users handling sensitive data. While it does not prevent all effects of prompt injections, it reduces potential exfiltration pathways.
doc_summary: OpenAI has launched a new security feature called Lockdown Mode for ChatGPT to mitigate the risk of data exfiltration from prompt injection attacks. This feature is available for personal accounts and business plans, providing advanced security settings that limit tools and capabilities connecting to the web or external services. Lockdown Mode aims to reduce outbound network requests, enhancing protection for sensitive data. It builds on sandboxing and existing controls to combat URL-based data exfiltration mechanisms. OpenAI also introduced an account management feature to review active sessions and detect unauthorized activity. The feature is not intended for everyone and cannot be used simultaneously with Developer Mode. Despite these measures, OpenAI acknowledges that Lockdown Mode does not guarantee complete prevention of data exfiltration or other effects of prompt injection attacks.
kill_chain_summary: The introduction of Lockdown Mode by OpenAI addresses the risk of data exfiltration through prompt injection attacks. By limiting outbound network requests, the feature aims to reduce the attack surface. However, it does not guarantee complete prevention, as other effects of prompt injections may still occur.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: OpenAI's Lockdown Mode targets the reduction of data exfiltration risks by limiting outbound network requests. diamond_model_summary: The incident involves unknown adversaries exploiting a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-3300, in the Everest Forms Pro plugin. The capability includes executing arbitrary PHP code via the plugin's Complex Calculation feature. The infrastructure involves specific IP addresses used for attacks. Victims are WordPress websites using vulnerable plugin versions.
doc_summary: Hackers are exploiting a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-3300, in the Everest Forms Pro plugin, affecting versions 1.9.12 and earlier. This vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on WordPress servers without authentication. The flaw resides in the Complex Calculation feature, which improperly sanitizes user input, enabling PHP code injection via the eval() function. Attackers create rogue administrator accounts, such as 'diksimarina', to gain full control over websites. Wordfence detected active exploitation starting April 13, blocking over 29,300 attempts. The attacks primarily originate from IPs 202.56.2[.]126 and 209.146.60.26. A patch was released on March 18, but exploitation continues.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of CVE-2026-3300, allowing adversaries to execute arbitrary code on WordPress servers. This leads to the installation of rogue admin accounts, granting full control over the websites. The attackers can then perform actions on objectives, such as modifying content and accessing sensitive data.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses used for attacks and the TTPs of code injection and privilege escalation. Title: Exploitation of CVE-2026-28318 in SolarWinds Serv-U

Victim.Description: Potentially affected SolarWinds Serv-U users

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a denial-of-service vulnerability in SolarWinds Serv-U, tracked as CVE-2026-28318. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the service using specially crafted POST requests with 'Content-Encoding: deflate'. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added this flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, indicating active exploitation. The issue has been addressed in SolarWinds Serv-U version 15.5.4 HF1, and mitigations include limiting access to known addresses and blocking requests containing 'content-encoding'.
doc_summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added a high-severity security flaw impacting SolarWinds Serv-U multi-protocol file server software to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-28318, is a denial-of-service (DoS) bug causing the service to crash under certain conditions. CISA described it as an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability resulting in a DoS condition. SolarWinds Serv-U is susceptible to specially crafted POST requests that crash the Serv-U service without authentication using Content-Encoding: deflate. The issue has been addressed in SolarWinds Serv-U version 15.5.4 HF1. Mitigations include limiting access to known addresses and blocking requests containing 'content-encoding'. CISA has ordered Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to address the flaw by June 19, 2026. In the past, multiple flaws in Serv-U have been exploited by bad actors, including those associated with the Cl0p ransomware gang.
kill_chain_summary: The exploitation of CVE-2026-28318 in SolarWinds Serv-U represents a significant threat, primarily affecting the exploitation stage of the MITRE ATT&CK kill chain. The vulnerability allows attackers to perform a denial-of-service attack by sending specially crafted POST requests with 'Content-Encoding: deflate', leading to uncontrolled resource consumption and service crashes. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has recognized this vulnerability as actively exploited, prompting immediate remediation actions. The exploitation stage is critical, as it directly impacts the availability of the targeted service.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident primarily involves the exploitation of a specific vulnerability, CVE-2026-28318, in SolarWinds Serv-U. The attack vector involves sending specially crafted POST requests with 'Content-Encoding: deflate', leading to a denial-of-service condition. While no specific IP addresses, domains, or hash values are identified, the focus is on the TTPs associated with exploiting this vulnerability. The remediation efforts include updating to a patched version and implementing network-level mitigations to block malicious requests. The lack of specific indicators like IPs or domains limits the Pyramid of Pain's applicability in this case.

Title: Miasma Supply Chain Attack on Microsoft GitHub Repositories

Victim.Description: The victims were Microsoft GitHub repositories, specifically Azure, Azure-Samples, Microsoft, and MicrosoftDocs.

diamond_model_summary: The Miasma supply chain attack on Microsoft GitHub repositories involved the adversary TeamPCP, who utilized the Miasma variant of the Mini Shai-Hulud worm. The attack targeted Microsoft's Azure, Azure-Samples, Microsoft, and MicrosoftDocs repositories, exploiting the trust model of open-source ecosystems. The adversary's capability included the use of the Bun loader for persistence, and the infrastructure involved GitHub and PyPI. The victims were primarily in the technology sector, with a high impact severity due to the widespread use of affected repositories.
doc_summary: Microsoft's GitHub repositories were targeted by the Miasma self-replicating supply chain attack, impacting 73 repositories across Azure, Azure-Samples, Microsoft, and MicrosoftDocs. The attack involved the re-compromise of the durabletask PyPI package by TeamPCP, delivering an information stealer on Linux systems. Miasma, a variant of the Mini Shai-Hulud worm, bypassed the npm registry, pushing malicious code directly to specific repositories. The attack exploited the trust model of open-source ecosystems, propagating across the ecosystem by compromising downstream users. The incident highlights the vulnerabilities in software delivery trust models, with Miasma operating within legitimate channels, making it difficult for conventional defenses to detect.
kill_chain_summary: The Miasma attack followed a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable repositories. Weaponization involved the creation of the Miasma variant, followed by delivery through compromised GitHub repositories. Exploitation targeted the trust model of open-source ecosystems, leading to installation of a payload runner. Command and control was maintained through GitHub repository persistence, and actions on objectives focused on propagating the worm and stealing information. The attack highlighted the vulnerabilities in software supply chains and the challenges in detecting malicious activity within legitimate channels.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Miasma attack presents significant challenges across the Pyramid of Pain. Hash values and IP addresses are less impactful due to the worm's ability to mutate and bypass traditional detection methods. Domain names and network host artifacts are also difficult to track due to the use of legitimate channels. Tools like the Bun loader and TTPs such as supply chain compromise are critical indicators, but the attack's reliance on exploiting trust models makes it particularly challenging to defend against. The attack underscores the need for enhanced supply chain security measures and monitoring of legitimate channels for malicious activity.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves UNC5221, a Chinese espionage group also known as VerdantBamboo, targeting Microsoft 365 environments using advanced malware like Brickstorm and Plenet. The adversary's capability includes exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities and using sophisticated malware implants. The infrastructure comprises compromised MSPs and SSL VPNs, with victims primarily in the technology sector in the United States. doc_summary: UNC5221, also known as VerdantBamboo, is a Chinese espionage group that has been exploiting Microsoft 365 environments using the Brickstorm backdoor and previously undocumented malware named Plenet and AgentPSD. The group gained access to victim networks at least 18 months before detection and compromised managed services providers (MSPs). They have been involved in attacks exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in edge devices since 2023. Brickstorm, described as an advanced malware implant, was initially written in Golang and later in Rust. In April 2024, Google documented UNC5221's activity using Brickstorm against legal services, SaaS providers, business process outsourcers, and technology companies. CISA warned about Brickstorm's deployment by Chinese hackers, and Google reported its use against Dell RecoverPoint for Virtual Machines. Volexity researchers found VerdantBamboo compromised an Egnyte Storage Sync system and accessed it through the victim's web SSL VPN. The attackers used Brickstorm's proxying features and stolen credentials to access Microsoft 365 environments. They spent at least 18 months on the network before detection and breached the organization again after remediation efforts. In the second intrusion, they used stolen credentials to enable SSL VPN access on the victim's firewall, connected to internal systems, and deployed custom malware to a Synology NAS device. Volexity concluded that the firewall and Storage Sync system were compromised at least 18 months earlier. Brickstorm was deployed to the victim's Egnyte Storage Sync appliance and a retired Linux GroupWise email archive server. The attackers deployed Plenet, a cross-platform .NET-based backdoor, to a Synology NAS appliance. Plenet, also known as Grimbolt, offers interactive shell access, remote command execution, file manipulation, and C2 server switching. AgentPSD, a Python-based reverse shell utility, was used as a fallback persistence mechanism. Volexity created a fingerprint to identify IP addresses and domains used for C2 communication, but the threat actor took the infrastructure offline before further systems could be revealed. Volexity describes VerdantBamboo as a highly sophisticated threat actor mixing living-off-the-land techniques and malware, targeting systems without EDR solutions.
kill_chain_summary: The attack by UNC5221 follows a structured kill chain, starting with the exploitation of zero-day vulnerabilities in edge devices for initial access. The adversary then installs malware like Brickstorm and Plenet for persistence and command and control. The use of WebSocket protocol for C2 communication highlights their evasion tactics. Finally, the attackers achieve their objectives by accessing and exfiltrating sensitive information from victim networks, demonstrating a high level of sophistication and persistence.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes various indicators such as malware families (Brickstorm, Plenet, AgentPSD) and communication protocols (WebSocket). The adversary's use of advanced malware and zero-day exploits presents significant challenges for detection and response. The infrastructure, including compromised MSPs and SSL VPNs, further complicates the detection process. The incident highlights the need for robust detection mechanisms and threat intelligence to counter sophisticated threat actors like UNC5221.

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), along with the FBI, NSA, and Department of Energy, issued a joint advisory warning critical infrastructure organizations about these ongoing attacks. Iranian hackers have been linked to previous breaches of ATG systems, manipulating display readings without altering actual fuel levels. The advisory recommends restricting remote access, replacing default passwords, applying security updates, and implementing multi-factor authentication to mitigate risks.

Title: PCPJack Hijacks Cloud Servers for Covert SMTP Relay Network

Victim.Description: Compromised business servers across multiple regions.

diamond_model_summary: PCPJack is a sophisticated threat actor that hijacked cloud servers from major providers like AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure to create a covert SMTP relay network. The infrastructure includes a C2 server with open directories, Sliver and Chisel tools, and deployer scripts for Linux beacons. The operation's end goal remains unclear, but it supports large-scale email delivery.
doc_summary: The threat actor PCPJack has hijacked cloud servers from Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure to create a covert SMTP email relay network. Compromised business servers across the United States, Europe, and Asia were converted into SMTP proxies. Hunt.io discovered source code, binaries, and a live Sliver configuration on an open C2 server. PCPJack was first identified by SentinelOne in April 2026, targeting cloud services with a credential theft framework. The infrastructure includes a Sliver-integrated SMTP proxy deployment toolkit, Chisel tunneling binaries, and deployer scripts for Linux beacons. The C2 server runs a Python script to verify Chisel tunnel ports for SMTP capability. Verified proxies are enriched with IP address data and synced to a downstream server. The operation's end goal remains unclear, but the infrastructure supports large-scale email delivery.
kill_chain_summary: PCPJack's attack involved reconnaissance to identify vulnerable cloud servers, weaponization through tool development, delivery of malicious binaries, exploitation of cloud server vulnerabilities, installation of persistence mechanisms, command and control via a C2 server, and actions on objectives by relaying SMTP traffic. The operation is sophisticated and opportunistic, leveraging compromised infrastructure for unknown purposes.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: PCPJack's operation involves several indicators of compromise, including IP addresses of C2 servers, domain names used for SMTP relay, and tools like Sliver and Chisel. These indicators are critical for detection and remediation efforts. The operation's complexity and use of cloud infrastructure highlight the need for robust monitoring and defensive measures.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a supply chain attack on Hola Browser, resulting in the delivery of a Monero cryptocurrency miner. doc_summary: The Windows version of Hola Browser, developed by the Israeli company Hola, was compromised in a supply chain attack. This attack delivered an undeclared executable identified as a Monero cryptocurrency miner. The compromise was discovered during AppEsteem certification checks. The miner, named 'me.exe', was found in the installation directory and was not certified, digitally signed, or timestamped. It added a Windows Defender exclusion rule, copied itself as 'HolaMonitorService.exe', and created an auto-starting Windows service. Hola confirmed the supply chain compromise, affecting about 0.1% of users, with no evidence of data theft. The company has since rebuilt its distribution pipeline and implemented advanced security measures. The incident was independently detected by cybersecurity firm Sygnia.
kill_chain_summary: The attack on Hola Browser follows a supply chain compromise model. The delivery stage involved the distribution of a malicious executable through Hola's update mechanism. Installation was achieved by creating an auto-starting Windows service. The final stage, actions on objectives, involved resource hijacking for cryptocurrency mining. Detection and remediation efforts focus on monitoring unauthorized services and unusual resource usage.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the identification of specific malware filenames such as 'me.exe' and 'HolaMonitorService.exe'. Title: IronWorm Supply-Chain Attack on npm Packages

Victim.Description: Victims include developers and CI environments using infected npm packages.

diamond_model_summary: The IronWorm supply-chain attack on npm packages demonstrates a sophisticated adversary using Rust-based malware with eBPF rootkit capabilities. The attack targets developers and CI environments, leveraging stolen credentials to propagate trojanized packages. The infrastructure includes Tor for C2 communication, and the attack was initiated from a compromised npm account. The adversary's motivation appears to be financial, with a focus on credential theft and potential cryptocurrency access.
doc_summary: IronWorm is a Rust-based infostealer malware involved in a supply-chain attack on the Node Package Manager (npm) index, infecting 36 packages. It targets environment variables and credential files, including those for OpenAI, AWS, Anthropic, and npm. The malware uses an eBPF kernel rootkit for stealth and communicates over the Tor network. It self-propagates by exploiting stolen npm credentials, compromising developer and CI environments to publish trojanized packages. The attack was initiated from a compromised account named 'asteroiddao' and involved malicious commits with timestamps altered to evade detection. Although no direct link to Shai Hulud was found, similar commit names suggest a possible evolution of TeamPCP's payload. The attack was detected early and mitigated before spreading to more popular npm packages. Developers are advised to upgrade to fixed releases, rotate keys, and enable two-factor authentication. A similar attack involving JavaScript-based malware named binding.gyp was also observed.
kill_chain_summary: The IronWorm attack follows a structured kill chain, beginning with the weaponization of Rust-based malware equipped with an eBPF rootkit. Delivery occurs through compromised npm packages, exploiting stolen credentials to execute and install trojanized packages in developer environments. Command and control is maintained via the Tor network, while actions on objectives focus on credential theft and malware propagation. The attack was detected early, preventing widespread impact.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The IronWorm attack presents challenges across the Pyramid of Pain, with the use of unique malware hashes, Tor-based C2 infrastructure, and advanced rootkit techniques. Detection and response require identifying specific indicators such as compromised npm packages and altered commit timestamps. The attack's sophistication and use of stealth tactics highlight the need for robust monitoring and incident response capabilities.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager, specifically a server-side request forgery that allows unauthenticated attackers to write files and escalate privileges to root. The adversary's capability is enhanced by the public availability of a proof-of-concept exploit. The infrastructure at risk includes systems running the WebDialer service, which is off by default but may be enabled in some deployments. Victims are organizations using Cisco Unified CM with WebDialer enabled, facing critical impact due to potential root access.
doc_summary: Cisco has patched a critical vulnerability in its Unified Communications Manager (CVE-2026-20230) that allows unauthenticated attackers to write files to the system and escalate privileges to root. The flaw is a server-side request forgery, and a proof-of-concept exploit is publicly available. The vulnerability is only exploitable when the WebDialer service is running, which is off by default. Cisco has released a patch for version 14 (14SU6), but the fix for version 15 is not due until September 2026. The flaw is similar to previous vulnerabilities in Cisco's voice products, such as CVE-2025-20309 and CVE-2026-20045.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves exploitation of a server-side request forgery vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager, allowing attackers to gain initial access and escalate privileges to root. The exploitation stage is critical, with a CVSS score of 8.6, and the public availability of a proof-of-concept exploit increases the risk. Detection focuses on monitoring unusual HTTP requests and unauthorized file writes, while remediation involves applying patches and disabling the WebDialer service if not needed.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident is primarily focused on the TTPs, as the vulnerability CVE-2026-20230 represents a significant threat due to its potential for root access escalation. The public availability of a proof-of-concept exploit increases the difficulty of defense, as adversaries can easily replicate the attack. Detection and remediation efforts should focus on monitoring HTTP requests and applying patches to mitigate the risk.

Title: Dismantling of Online Marketplace for Fake Identity Documents in the EU

Victim.Description: European Union member states affected by document fraud.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves an adversary operating an online marketplace for counterfeit identity documents, targeting the European Union. The capability includes document-production equipment, and the infrastructure is an online platform. The victim is the EU, with government sectors affected by document fraud.
doc_summary: French and Spanish authorities dismantled an online marketplace selling fake identity documents to migrant smuggling rings within the European Union. On May 27, law enforcement arrested a suspect in Alicante, Spain, seizing document-production equipment and approximately 800 counterfeit European identity documents. The investigation began after French authorities identified a website advertising counterfeit identity documents, tracing the suspect to Alicante. The suspect allegedly administered a marketplace offering forged identity and administrative documents to customers across Europe, facilitating migrant smuggling operations by supplying criminal networks with fraudulent documents to evade border controls and obtain residence rights. Europol expanded its capacity to combat migrant smuggling in March 2026, following a 2025 EU Serious and Organised Crime Threat Assessment that flagged document fraud as a main enabler of fraudulent legalization of residency and migrant smuggling within the EU.

doc_summary: Cisco has released a critical security update for a vulnerability in the Unified Communications Manager (Unified CM), previously known as Cisco CallManager. This flaw allows attackers to gain root privileges through a low-complexity server-side request forgery (SSRF) attack. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-20230, can be exploited remotely without privileges. Cisco's Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) is aware of publicly available proof-of-concept exploit code but has not found evidence of active exploitation. The vulnerability affects systems with the WebDialer service enabled, which is disabled by default. Administrators are advised to install Cisco Unified CM versions 14SU6 or 15SU5 and can disable the WebDialer service as a temporary measure. The vulnerability has been assigned a Security Impact Rating (SIR) of Critical.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves the exploitation stage, where attackers leverage a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager to gain root privileges.
